द्विजानां वीरुधां चैव नक्षत्रग्रहयोस् तथा
यज्ञानां तपसां चैव सोमं राज्ये ऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
Over the twice-born, the plants, and the asterisms and planets,
and over sacrifices and austerities, he consecrated Soma in sovereignty.

4.s:
apāṃ tu varuṇaṃ rājye rājñāṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ patim
ādityānāṃ tathā viṣṇuṃ vasūnām atha pāvakam //
4.d:
अपां तु वरुणं राज्ये राज्ञां वैश्रवणं पतिम्
आदित्यानां तथा विष्णुं वसूनाम् अथ पावकम् ॥
4.m:
Varuṇa he placed in sovereignty over the waters, and Vaiśravaṇa as lord over kings,
Viṣṇu likewise over the Ādityas, and Pāvaka over the Vasus;

4.s:
prajāpatīnāṃ dakṣaṃ tu marutām atha vāsavam
daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ vai prahrādam amitaujasam //
4.d:
प्रजापतीनां दक्षं तु मरुताम् अथ वासवम्
दैत्यानां दानवानां वै प्रह्रादम् अमितौजसम् ॥
4.m:
Dakṣa over the lords of creatures, and Vāsava over the Maruts;
Prahrāda of boundless splendor over the Daityas and Dānavas;

4.s:
vaivasvataṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca yamaṃ rājye 'bhyaṣecayat
yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca pārthivānāṃ tathaiva ca //
4.d:
वैवस्वतं पितॄणां च यमं राज्ये ऽभ्यषेचयत्
यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च पार्थिवानां तथैव च ॥
4.m:
and Yama, son of Vivasvat, he consecrated to kingship over the ancestors,
and likewise over the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and earthly kings;

4.s:
sarvabhūtapiśācānāṃ girīśaṃ śūlapāṇinam
śailānāṃ himavantaṃ ca nadīnām atha sāgaram //
4.d:
सर्वभूतपिशाचानां गिरीशं शूलपाणिनम्
शैलानां हिमवन्तं च नदीनाम् अथ सागरम् ॥
4.m:
Girīśa, the spear-wielder, over all ghosts and Piśācas;
Himavat over mountains, and the ocean over rivers;

4.s:
gandharvāṇām adhipatiṃ cakre citrarathaṃ prabhum
nāgānāṃ vāsukiṃ cakre sarpāṇām atha takṣakam //
4.d:
गन्धर्वाणाम् अधिपतिं चक्रे चित्ररथं प्रभुम्
नागानां वासुकिं चक्रे सर्पाणाम् अथ तक्षकम् ॥
4.m:
Citraratha the lord he made ruler over the Gandharvas;
Vāsuki he made ruler over Nāgas, and Takṣaka over serpents;

4.s:
vāraṇānāṃ tu rājānam airāvatam athādiśat
uccaiḥśravasam aśvānāṃ garuḍaṃ caiva pakṣiṇām //
4.d:
वारणानां तु राजानम् ऐरावतम् अथादिशत्
उच्चैःश्रवसम् अश्वानां गरुडं चैव पक्षिणाम् ॥
4.m:
Airāvata he appointed king over elephants,
Uccaiḥśravas over horses, and Garuḍa over birds;

4.s:
mṛgāṇām atha śārdūlaṃ govṛṣaṃ tu gavāṃ patim
vanaspatīnāṃ rājānaṃ plakṣam evābhyaṣecayat //
4.d:
मृगाणाम् अथ शार्दूलं गोवृषं तु गवां पतिम्
वनस्पतीनां राजानं प्लक्षम् एवाभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
the tiger over wild beasts, the bull as lord of cattle,
and the Plakṣa tree alone he consecrated as king of trees.

4.s:
evaṃ vibhajya rājyāni krameṇaiva pitāmahaḥ
diśāṃ pālān atha tataḥ sthāpayām āsa sa prabhuḥ //
4.d:
एवं विभज्य राज्यानि क्रमेणैव पितामहः
दिशां पालान् अथ ततः स्थापयाम् आस स प्रभुः ॥
4.m:
Having thus divided the realms in succession, the Grandfather,
that powerful lord, then established the guardians of the directions.

4.s:
pūrvasyāṃ diśi putraṃ tu vairājasya prajāpateḥ
diśaḥ pālaṃ sudhanvānaṃ rājānaṃ so 'bhyaṣecayat //
4.d:
पूर्वस्यां दिशि पुत्रं तु वैराजस्य प्रजापतेः
दिशः पालं सुधन्वानं राजानं सो ऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
In the eastern direction he consecrated King Sudhanvan,
son of the lord of creatures Vairāja, as guardian of the quarter.

4.s:
dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi tathā kardamasya prajāpateḥ
putraṃ śaṅkhapadaṃ nāma rājānaṃ so 'bhyaṣecayat //
4.d:
दक्षिणस्यां दिशि तथा कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः
पुत्रं शङ्खपदं नाम राजानं सो ऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
In the southern direction likewise he consecrated King Śaṅkhapada,
son of the lord of creatures Kardama.

4.s:
paścimasyāṃ diśi tathā rajasaḥ putram acyutam
ketumantaṃ mahātmānaṃ rājānaṃ so 'bhyaṣecayat //
4.d:
पश्चिमस्यां दिशि तथा रजसः पुत्रम् अच्युतम्
केतुमन्तं महात्मानं राजानं सो ऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
In the western direction likewise he consecrated the noble King Ketumant,
the imperishable son of Rajas.

4.s:
tathā hiraṇyaromāṇaṃ parjanyasya prajāpateḥ
udīcyāṃ diśi durdharṣaṃ rājānaṃ so 'bhyaṣecayat //
4.d:
तथा हिरण्यरोमाणं पर्जन्यस्य प्रजापतेः
उदीच्यां दिशि दुर्धर्षं राजानं सो ऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥
4.m:
Likewise, in the northern direction he consecrated King Hiraṇyaroman,
the unassailable son of the lord of creatures Parjanya.

4.s:
tair iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā
yathāpradeśam adyāpi dharmeṇa pratipālyate //
4.d:
तैर् इयं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना
यथाप्रदेशम् अद्यापि धर्मेण प्रतिपाल्यते ॥
4.m:
By them this entire earth, with its seven continents and its cities,
is protected according to dharma in each region even today.

4.s:
rājasūyābhiṣiktas tu pṛthur etair narādhipaiḥ
vedadṛṣṭena vidhinā rājā rājye narādhipaḥ //
4.d:
राजसूयाभिषिक्तस् तु पृथुर् एतैर् नराधिपैः
वेददृष्टेन विधिना राजा राज्ये नराधिपः ॥
4.m:
And Pṛthu was consecrated by the rājasūya rite by these rulers of men
according to the ordinance revealed in the Veda, a king over kingship, a lord of men.

4.s:
tato manvantare 'tīte cākṣuṣe 'mitatejasi
vaivasvatāya manave pṛthivyāṃ rājyam ādiśat //
4.d:
ततो मन्वन्तरे ऽतीते चाक्षुषे ऽमिततेजसि
वैवस्वताय मनवे पृथिव्यां राज्यम् आदिशत् ॥
4.m:
Then, when the Cākṣuṣa manvantara of boundless splendor had passed,
he appointed the sovereignty over the earth to Manu Vaivasvata.

4.s:
tasya vistaram ākhyāsye manor vaivasvatasya ha
bhavatāṃ cānukūlyāya yadi śrotum ihecchatha
mahad etad adhiṣṭhānaṃ purāṇe tad adhiṣṭhitam //
4.d:
तस्य विस्तरम् आख्यास्ये मनोर् वैवस्वतस्य ह
भवतां चानुकूल्याय यदि श्रोतुम् इहेच्छथ
महद् एतद् अधिष्ठानं पुराणे तद् अधिष्ठितम् ॥

4.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
vistareṇa pṛthor janma lomaharṣaṇa kīrtaya
yathā mahātmanā tena dugdhā veyaṃ vasuṃdharā //
4.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
विस्तरेण पृथोर् जन्म लोमहर्षण कीर्तय
यथा महात्मना तेन दुग्धा वेयं वसुंधरा ॥

4.s:
yathā vāpi nṛbhir dugdhā yathā devair maharṣibhiḥ
yathā daityaiś ca nāgaiś ca yathā yakṣair yathā drumaiḥ //
4.d:
यथा वापि नृभिर् दुग्धा यथा देवैर् महर्षिभिः
यथा दैत्यैश् च नागैश् च यथा यक्षैर् यथा द्रुमैः ॥
4.m:
or how she was milked by men, by the gods, and by the great sages,
how by the Daityas and the Nāgas, how by the Yakṣas, how by the trees,

4.s:
yathā śailaiḥ piśācaiś ca gandharvaiś ca dvijottamaiḥ
rākṣasaiś ca mahāsattvair yathā dugdhā vasuṃdharā //
4.d:
यथा शैलैः पिशाचैश् च गन्धर्वैश् च द्विजोत्तमैः
राक्षसैश् च महासत्त्वैर् यथा दुग्धा वसुंधरा ॥
4.m:
how by the mountains and Piśācas, by the Gandharvas and best of the twice-born,
and how the earth was milked by the Rākṣasas of great vigor;

4.s:
teṣāṃ pātraviśeṣāṃś ca vaktum arhasi suvrata
vatsakṣīraviśeṣāṃś ca dogdhāraṃ cānupūrvaśaḥ //
4.d:
तेषां पात्रविशेषांश् च वक्तुम् अर्हसि सुव्रत
वत्सक्षीरविशेषांश् च दोग्धारं चानुपूर्वशः ॥
4.m:
and you should tell their particular vessels, O one of good vows,
the differences of calves and milk, and the milkers in due order,

4.s:
yasmāc ca kāraṇāt pāṇir veṇasya mathitaḥ purā
kruddhair maharṣibhis tāta kāraṇaṃ tac ca kīrtaya //
4.d:
यस्माच् च कारणात् पाणिर् वेणस्य मथितः पुरा
क्रुद्धैर् महर्षिभिस् तात कारणं तच् च कीर्तय ॥
4.m:
and the reason why Vena's hand was churned in former times
by the enraged great sages; O venerable one, narrate that cause as well.

4.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi pṛthor vaiṇyasya vistaram
ekāgrāḥ prayatāś caiva puṇyārthaṃ vai dvijarṣabhāḥ //
4.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
शृणुध्वं कीर्तयिष्यामि पृथोर् वैण्यस्य विस्तरम्
एकाग्राः प्रयताश् चैव पुण्यार्थं वै द्विजर्षभाः ॥
4.m:
Lomaharṣaṇa said:
Listen, I shall relate in detail about Pṛthu, son of Vena,
with one-pointed minds and restrained, for the sake of merit, O best of the twice-born.

4.s:
nāśuceḥ kṣudramanaso nāśiṣyasyāvratasya ca
kīrtayeyam idaṃ viprāḥ kṛtaghnāyāhitāya ca //
4.d:
नाशुचेः क्षुद्रमनसो नाशिष्यस्याव्रतस्य च
कीर्तयेयम् इदं विप्राः कृतघ्नायाहिताय च ॥
4.m:
I would not recite this to one impure, to one of base mind, to a non-disciple, or to one without vows,
O learned priests, nor to the ungrateful or to one ill-disposed.

4.s:
svargyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ dhanyaṃ vedaiś ca saṃmitam
rahasyam ṛṣibhiḥ proktaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ vai yathātatham //
4.d:
स्वर्ग्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यं धन्यं वेदैश् च संमितम्
रहस्यम् ऋषिभिः प्रोक्तं शृणुध्वं वै यथातथम् ॥
4.m:
Securing heaven, bringing fame and long life, auspicious, equal to the Vedas,
it was spoken as a secret by the sages; hear it indeed as it truly is.

4.s:
yaś cemaṃ kīrtayen nityaṃ pṛthor vaiṇyasya vistaram
brāhmaṇebhyo namaskṛtya na sa śocet kṛtākṛtam //
4.d:
यश् चेमं कीर्तयेन् नित्यं पृथोर् वैण्यस्य विस्तरम्
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नमस्कृत्य न स शोचेत् कृताकृतम् ॥
4.m:
Whoever constantly recites this detailed account of Pṛthu, son of Vena,
having bowed to the brāhmaṇas, shall not grieve over what has been done or left undone.

4.s:
āsīd dharmasya saṃgoptā pūrvam atrisamaḥ prabhuḥ
atrivaṃśe samutpannas tv aṅgo nāma prajāpatiḥ //
4.d:
आसीद् धर्मस्य संगोप्ता पूर्वम् अत्रिसमः प्रभुः
अत्रिवंशे समुत्पन्नस् त्व् अङ्गो नाम प्रजापतिः ॥
4.m:
Formerly there was a lord, a protector of dharma equal to Atri,
a lord of creatures born in the lineage of Atri named Aṅga.

4.s:
tasya putro 'bhavad veṇo nātyarthaṃ dharmakovidaḥ
jāto mṛtyusutāyāṃ vai sunīthāyāṃ prajāpatiḥ //
4.d:
तस्य पुत्रो ऽभवद् वेणो नात्यर्थं धर्मकोविदः
जातो मृत्युसुतायां वै सुनीथायां प्रजापतिः ॥
4.m:
His son was Vena, who was not exceedingly skilled in dharma;
that lord of creatures was born of Sunīthā, daughter of Death.

4.s:
sa mātāmahadoṣeṇa tena kālātmajātmajaḥ
svadharmaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā kāmalobheṣv avartata //
4.d:
स मातामहदोषेण तेन कालात्मजात्मजः
स्वधर्मं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा कामलोभेष्व् अवर्तत ॥
4.m:
Through that flaw of his maternal grandfather, the son of the daughter of Death,
having turned his back on his own dharma, engaged in desire and greed.

4.s:
maryādāṃ bhedayām āsa dharmopetāṃ sa pārthivaḥ
vedadharmān atikramya so 'dharmanirato 'bhavat //
4.d:
मर्यादां भेदयाम् आस धर्मोपेतां स पार्थिवः
वेदधर्मान् अतिक्रम्य सो ऽधर्मनिरतो ऽभवत् ॥
4.m:
That king broke the boundary accompanied by dharma;
transgressing the Vedic dharmas, he became devoted to adharma.

4.s:
niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkārāḥ prajās tasmin prajāpatau
pravṛttaṃ na papuḥ somaṃ hutaṃ yajñeṣu devatāḥ //
4.d:
निःस्वाध्यायवषट्काराः प्रजास् तस्मिन् प्रजापतौ
प्रवृत्तं न पपुः सोमं हुतं यज्ञेषु देवताः ॥
4.m:
While that lord of creatures ruled, the subjects were without Vedic study and the vaṣaṭ-call;
the deities did not drink the offered soma poured out at sacrifices.

4.s:
na yaṣṭavyaṃ na hotavyam iti tasya prajāpateḥ
āsīt pratijñā krūreyaṃ vināśe pratyupasthite //
4.d:
न यष्टव्यं न होतव्यम् इति तस्य प्रजापतेः
आसीत् प्रतिज्ञा क्रूरेयं विनाशे प्रत्युपस्थिते ॥
4.m:
'No sacrifice is to be performed; no oblation is to be offered'—such was the cruel proclamation
of that lord of creatures when his destruction was at hand:

4.s:
aham ijyaś ca yaṣṭā ca yajñaś ceti bhṛgūdvaha
mayi yajño vidhātavyo mayi hotavyam ity api //
4.d:
अहम् इज्यश् च यष्टा च यज्ञश् चेति भृगूद्वह
मयि यज्ञो विधातव्यो मयि होतव्यम् इत्य् अपि ॥
4.m:
'I am the one to be worshipped, I am the sacrificer, and I am the sacrifice, O scion of Bhṛgu!
Sacrifice must be offered to me, and libation must be poured into me!'

4.s:
tam atikrāntamaryādam ādadānam asāṃpratam
ūcur maharṣayaḥ sarve marīcipramukhās tadā //
4.d:
तम् अतिक्रान्तमर्यादम् आददानम् असांप्रतम्
ऊचुर् महर्षयः सर्वे मरीचिप्रमुखास् तदा ॥
4.m:
When he had overstepped the boundary and took what was improper,
all the great sages, headed by Marīci, then spoke to him:

4.s:
vayaṃ dīkṣāṃ pravekṣyāmaḥ saṃvatsaragaṇān bahūn
adharmaṃ kuru mā veṇa eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
4.d:
वयं दीक्षां प्रवेक्ष्यामः संवत्सरगणान् बहून्
अधर्मं कुरु मा वेण एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥
4.m:
'We are about to enter upon consecration for many series of years;
do not commit adharma, Vena; this is the eternal dharma.

4.s:
nidhane 'treḥ prasūtas tvaṃ prajāpatir asaṃśayam
prajāś ca pālayiṣye 'ham itīha samayaḥ kṛtaḥ //
4.d:
निधने ऽत्रेः प्रसूतस् त्वं प्रजापतिर् असंशयम्
प्रजाश् च पालयिष्ये ऽहम् इतीह समयः कृतः ॥
4.m:
You were born in the lineage of Atri as an undoubted lord of creatures,
and your compact was made here: "I will protect the subjects."'

4.s:
tāṃs tathā bruvataḥ sarvān maharṣīn abravīt tadā
veṇaḥ prahasya durbuddhir imam artham anarthavit //
4.d:
तांस् तथा ब्रुवतः सर्वान् महर्षीन् अब्रवीत् तदा
वेणः प्रहस्य दुर्बुद्धिर् इमम् अर्थम् अनर्थवित् ॥
4.m:
To all the great sages speaking thus at that time,
Vena, evil-minded and ignorant of what is beneficial, laughed and said this:

4.s:
veṇa uvāca
sraṣṭā dharmasya kaś cānyaḥ śrotavyaṃ kasya vā mayā
śrutavīryatapaḥsatyair mayā vā kaḥ samo bhuvi //
4.d:
वेण उवाच
स्रष्टा धर्मस्य कश् चान्यः श्रोतव्यं कस्य वा मया
श्रुतवीर्यतपःसत्यैर् मया वा कः समो भुवि ॥
4.m:
Vena said:
'Who else is the creator of dharma, or whose word should I hear?
Or who on earth is my equal in sacred learning, prowess, austerity, and truth?

4.s:
prabhavaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
saṃmūḍhā na vidur nūnaṃ bhavanto māṃ vicetasaḥ //
4.d:
प्रभवं सर्वभूतानां धर्माणां च विशेषतः
संमूढा न विदुर् नूनं भवन्तो मां विचेतसः ॥
4.m:
Deluded and mindless as you are, you surely do not know me,
the source of all beings, and of dharmas especially!'

4.s:
icchan daheyaṃ pṛthivīṃ plāvayeyaṃ jalais tathā
dyāṃ vai bhuvaṃ ca rundheyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
4.d:
इच्छन् दहेयं पृथिवीं प्लावयेयं जलैस् तथा
द्यां वै भुवं च रुन्धेयं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
4.m: "If I wish, I could burn the earth, and likewise flood it with waters; / I could certainly block both heaven and earth; there should be no doubt about this."

4.s:
yadā na śakyate mohād avalepāc ca pārthivaḥ
apanetuṃ tadā veṇas tataḥ kruddhā maharṣayaḥ //
4.d:
यदा न शक्यते मोहाद् अवलेपाच् च पार्थिवः
अपनेतुं तदा वेणस् ततः क्रुद्धा महर्षयः ॥
4.m: When the king could not be diverted from his delusion and arrogance, / then the great sages became enraged at Veṇa.

4.s:
taṃ nigṛhya mahātmāno visphurantaṃ mahābalam
tato 'sya savyam ūruṃ te mamanthur jātamanyavaḥ //
4.d:
तं निगृह्य महात्मानो विस्फुरन्तं महाबलम्
ततो ऽस्य सव्यम् ऊरुं ते ममन्थुर् जातमन्यवः ॥
4.m: Those great-souled ones seized him, struggling and endowed with great strength; / then, their wrath aroused, they churned his left thigh.

4.s:
tasmin nimathyamāne vai rājña ūrau tu jajñivān
hrasvo 'timātraḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaś ceti babhūva ha //
4.d:
तस्मिन् निमथ्यमाने वै राज्ञ ऊरौ तु जज्ञिवान्
ह्रस्वो ऽतिमात्रः पुरुषः कृष्णश् चेति बभूव ह ॥
4.m: As that king's thigh was being churned, / there was born a man who was exceedingly short and black.

4.s:
sa bhītaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā tasthivān dvijasattamāḥ
tam atrir vihvalaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣīdety abravīt tadā //
4.d:
स भीतः प्राञ्जलिर् भूत्वा तस्थिवान् द्विजसत्तमाः
तम् अत्रिर् विह्वलं दृष्ट्वा निषीदेत्य् अब्रवीत् तदा ॥
4.m: Terrified, he stood with joined palms, O best of the twice-born; / seeing him agitated, Atri then said to him: "Sit down!" (niṣīda).

4.s:
niṣādavaṃśakartāsau babhūva vadatāṃ varāḥ
dhīvarān asṛjac cāpi veṇakalmaṣasaṃbhavān //
4.d:
निषादवंशकर्तासौ बभूव वदतां वराः
धीवरान् असृजच् चापि वेणकल्मषसंभवान् ॥
4.m: He became the founder of the Niṣāda lineage, O best of speakers; / he also produced the Dhīvaras, who arose from the sin of Veṇa,

4.s:
ye cānye vindhyanilayās tathā parvatasaṃśrayāḥ
adharmarucayo viprās te tu vai veṇakalmaṣāḥ //
4.d:
ये चान्ये विन्ध्यनिलयास् तथा पर्वतसंश्रयाः
अधर्मरुचयो विप्रास् ते तु वै वेणकल्मषाः ॥
4.m: as well as others who dwell in the Vindhya mountains and inhabit the hills, / who take pleasure in unrighteousness, O brahmins: these indeed arose from Veṇa's sin.

4.s:
tataḥ punar mahātmānaḥ pāṇiṃ veṇasya dakṣiṇam
araṇīm iva saṃrabdhā mamanthur jātamanyavaḥ //
4.d:
ततः पुनर् महात्मानः पाणिं वेणस्य दक्षिणम्
अरणीम् इव संरब्धा ममन्थुर् जातमन्यवः ॥
4.m: Then again the great-souled ones, their wrath aroused, excitedly churned / the right hand of Veṇa as though it were a fire-stick.

4.s:
pṛthus tasmāt samutpannaḥ karāj jvalanasaṃnibhaḥ
dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā sākṣād agnir iva jvalan //
4.d:
पृथुस् तस्मात् समुत्पन्नः कराज् ज्वलनसंनिभः
दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा साक्षाद् अग्निर् इव ज्वलन् ॥
4.m: From that hand Pṛthu was born, resembling a blazing fire, / shining with his own body like fire itself blazing in visible form.

4.s:
atha so 'jagavaṃ nāma dhanur gṛhya mahāravam
śarāṃś ca divyān rakṣārthaṃ kavacaṃ ca mahāprabham //
4.d:
अथ सो ऽजगवं नाम धनुर् गृह्य महारवम्
शरांश् च दिव्यान् रक्षार्थं कवचं च महाप्रभम् ॥
4.m: Then, seizing the loud-sounding bow named Ājagava, / along with divine arrows for protection and a magnificent armor of great splendor,

4.s:
tasmiñ jāte 'tha bhūtāni saṃprahṛṣṭāni sarvaśaḥ
samāpetur mahābhāgā veṇas tu tridivaṃ yayau //
4.d:
तस्मिञ् जाते ऽथ भूतानि संप्रहृष्टानि सर्वशः
समापेतुर् महाभागा वेणस् तु त्रिदिवं ययौ ॥
4.m: when he was born, all creatures rejoiced completely / and gathered together, O fortunate ones; but Veṇa departed to heaven.

4.s:
samutpannena bho viprāḥ satputreṇa mahātmanā
trātaḥ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ puṃnāmno narakāt tadā //
4.d:
समुत्पन्नेन भो विप्राः सत्पुत्रेण महात्मना
त्रातः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः पुंनाम्नो नरकात् तदा ॥
4.m: By that great-souled, virtuous son who had arisen, O brahmins, / that tiger among men was then saved from the hell named Put.

4.s:
taṃ samudrāś ca nadyaś ca ratnāny ādāya sarvaśaḥ
toyāni cābhiṣekārthaṃ sarva evopatasthire //
4.d:
तं समुद्राश् च नद्यश् च रत्नान्य् आदाय सर्वशः
तोयानि चाभिषेकार्थं सर्व एवोपतस्थिरे ॥
4.m: The oceans and rivers, bringing jewels from all around / and waters for consecration, all approached him.

4.s:
pitāmahaś ca bhagavān devair āṅgirasaiḥ saha
sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni jaṅgamāni ca sarvaśaḥ //
4.d:
पितामहश् च भगवान् देवैर् आङ्गिरसैः सह
स्थावराणि च भूतानि जङ्गमानि च सर्वशः ॥
4.m: And the venerable grandfather [Brahmā], along with the Āṅgirasa gods, / and all stationary and moving creatures from every side,

4.s:
samāgamya tadā vaiṇyam abhyaṣiñcan narādhipam
mahatā rājarājena prajās tenānurañjitāḥ //
4.d:
समागम्य तदा वैण्यम् अभ्यषिञ्चन् नराधिपम्
महता राजराजेन प्रजास् तेनानुरञ्जिताः ॥
4.m: having assembled, then consecrated the son of Veṇa as ruler of men; / by that great king of kings the subjects were gladdened.

4.s:
so 'bhiṣikto mahātejā vidhivad dharmakovidaiḥ
ādhirājye tadā rājñāṃ pṛthur vaiṇyaḥ pratāpavān //
4.d:
सो ऽभिषिक्तो महातेजा विधिवद् धर्मकोविदैः
आधिराज्ये तदा राज्ञां पृथुर् वैण्यः प्रतापवान् ॥
4.m: He, endowed with great fiery energy and valor, Pṛthu the son of Veṇa, / was then duly consecrated to sovereignty over kings by those skilled in dharma.

4.s:
pitrāparañjitās tasya prajās tenānurañjitāḥ
anurāgāt tatas tasya nāma rājābhyajāyata //
4.d:
पित्रापरञ्जितास् तस्य प्रजास् तेनानुरञ्जिताः
अनुरागात् ततस् तस्य नाम राजाभ्यजायत ॥
4.m: His subjects, alienated by his father, were delighted by him; / on account of that affection (anurāga), the name "king" (rājā) arose for him.

4.s:
āpas tastambhire tasya samudram abhiyāsyataḥ
parvatāś ca dadur mārgaṃ dhvajabhaṅgaś ca nābhavat //
4.d:
आपस् तस्तम्भिरे तस्य समुद्रम् अभियास्यतः
पर्वताश् च ददुर् मार्गं ध्वजभङ्गश् च नाभवत् ॥
4.m: The waters solidified for him when he marched to the ocean; / the mountains made way, and no banner of his was ever broken.

4.s:
akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī sidhyanty annāni cintanāt
sarvakāmadughā gāvaḥ puṭake puṭake madhu //
4.d:
अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी सिध्यन्त्य् अन्नानि चिन्तनात्
सर्वकामदुघा गावः पुटके पुटके मधु ॥
4.m: The earth ripened crops without plowing; food was accomplished merely by thought; / the cows yielded every desire, and there was honey in every leaf-cup.

4.s:
etasminn eva kāle tu yajñe paitāmahe śubhe
sūtaḥ sūtyāṃ samutpannaḥ sautye 'hani mahāmatiḥ //
4.d:
एतस्मिन्न् एव काले तु यज्ञे पैतामहे शुभे
सूतः सूत्यां समुत्पन्नः सौत्ये ऽहनि महामतिः ॥
4.m: At that very time, at an auspicious sacrifice of the grandfather [Brahmā], / the wise bard was born from the pressing of soma on the soma-pressing day.

4.s:
tasminn eva mahāyajñe jajñe prājño 'tha māgadhaḥ
pṛthoḥ stavārthaṃ tau tatra samāhūtau maharṣibhiḥ //
4.d:
तस्मिन्न् एव महायज्ञे जज्ञे प्राज्ञो ऽथ मागधः
पृथोः स्तवार्थं तौ तत्र समाहूतौ महर्षिभिः ॥
4.m: At that very great sacrifice the wise Māgadha was also born; / in order to praise Pṛthu, the two were summoned there by the great sages.

4.s:
tāv ūcur ṛṣayaḥ sarve stūyatām eṣa pārthivaḥ
karmaitad anurūpaṃ vāṃ pātraṃ cāyaṃ narādhipaḥ //
4.d:
ताव् ऊचुर् ऋषयः सर्वे स्तूयताम् एष पार्थिवः
कर्मैतद् अनुरूपं वां पात्रं चायं नराधिपः ॥
4.m: All the sages said to them: "Let this king be praised! / This deed is suitable for you two, and this ruler of men is a worthy recipient."

4.s:
tāv ūcatus tadā sarvāṃs tān ṛṣīn sūtamāgadhau
āvāṃ devān ṛṣīṃś caiva prīṇayāvaḥ svakarmabhiḥ //
4.d:
ताव् ऊचतुस् तदा सर्वांस् तान् ऋषीन् सूतमागधौ
आवां देवान् ऋषींश् चैव प्रीणयावः स्वकर्मभिः ॥
4.m: Then the bard and the Māgadha said to all those sages: / "We two gratify the gods and the sages by our own deeds;

4.s:
na cāsya vidmo vai karma nāma vā lakṣaṇaṃ yaśaḥ
stotraṃ yenāsya kuryāva rājñas tejasvino dvijāḥ //
4.d:
न चास्य विद्मो वै कर्म नाम वा लक्षणं यशः
स्तोत्रं येनास्य कुर्याव राज्ञस् तेजस्विनो द्विजाः ॥
4.m: we do not know his deed, name, characteristic mark, or fame / by which we might compose a eulogy for this fiery king, O twice-born."

4.s:
ṛṣibhis tau niyuktau tu bhaviṣyaiḥ stūyatām iti
yāni karmāṇi kṛtavān pṛthuḥ paścān mahābalaḥ //
4.d:
ऋषिभिस् तौ नियुक्तौ तु भविष्यैः स्तूयताम् इति
यानि कर्माणि कृतवान् पृथुः पश्चान् महाबलः ॥
4.m: The two were then instructed by the sages: "Let him be praised for future deeds! / For the deeds which the mighty Pṛthu will perform later."

4.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti vai loke staveṣu munisattamāḥ
āśīrvādāḥ prayujyante sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ //
4.d:
ततः प्रभृति वै लोके स्तवेषु मुनिसत्तमाः
आशीर्वादाः प्रयुज्यन्ते सूतमागधबन्दिभिः ॥
4.m: From then on in the world, O best of sages, in eulogies, / blessings are employed by bards, Māgadhas, and panegyrists.

4.s:
tayoḥ stavānte suprītaḥ pṛthuḥ prādāt prajeśvaraḥ
anūpadeśaṃ sūtāya magadhaṃ māgadhāya ca //
4.d:
तयोः स्तवान्ते सुप्रीतः पृथुः प्रादात् प्रजेश्वरः
अनूपदेशं सूताय मगधं मागधाय च ॥
4.m: At the conclusion of their praise, Pṛthu, the lord of creatures, well-pleased, granted / the wetland region to the bard, and Magadha to the Māgadha.

4.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītāḥ prajāḥ procur manīṣiṇaḥ
vṛttīnām eṣa vo dātā bhaviṣyati narādhipaḥ //
4.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीताः प्रजाः प्रोचुर् मनीषिणः
वृत्तीनाम् एष वो दाता भविष्यति नराधिपः ॥
4.m: Seeing him, the subjects, utterly delighted, said to the wise ones: / "This ruler of men shall be the giver of our livelihoods!"

4.s:
tato vaiṇyaṃ mahātmānaṃ prajāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ
tvaṃ no vṛttiṃ vidhatsveti maharṣivacanāt tadā //
4.d:
ततो वैण्यं महात्मानं प्रजाः समभिदुद्रुवुः
त्वं नो वृत्तिं विधत्स्वेति महर्षिवचनात् तदा ॥
4.m: Then, at the word of the great sages, the subjects / rushed toward the great-souled son of Veṇa, saying: "Ordain our livelihood!"

4.s:
so 'bhidrutaḥ prajābhis tu prajāhitacikīrṣayā
dhanur gṛhya pṛṣatkāṃś ca pṛthivīm ādravad balī //
4.d:
सो ऽभिद्रुतः प्रजाभिस् तु प्रजाहितचिकीर्षया
धनुर् गृह्य पृषत्कांश् च पृथिवीम् आद्रवद् बली ॥
4.m: Approached by the subjects, wishing to act for the welfare of his subjects, / the mighty one seized his bow and arrows and rushed against the earth.

4.s:
tato vaiṇyabhayatrastā gaur bhūtvā prādravan mahī
tāṃ pṛthur dhanur ādāya dravantīm anvadhāvata //
4.d:
ततो वैण्यभयत्रस्ता गौर् भूत्वा प्राद्रवन् मही
तां पृथुर् धनुर् आदाय द्रवन्तीम् अन्वधावत ॥
4.m: Then, terrified of the son of Veṇa, the earth assumed the form of a cow and ran away; / taking his bow, Pṛthu pursued her as she fled.

4.s:
sā lokān brahmalokādīn gatvā vaiṇyabhayāt tadā
pradadarśāgrato vaiṇyaṃ pragṛhītaśarāsanam //
4.d:
सा लोकान् ब्रह्मलोकादीन् गत्वा वैण्यभयात् तदा
प्रददर्शाग्रतो वैण्यं प्रगृहीतशरासनम् ॥
4.m: Having gone through the worlds beginning with the world of Brahmā out of fear of the son of Veṇa, / she saw the son of Veṇa before her, holding up his bow,

4.s:
jvaladbhir niśitair bāṇair dīptatejasam antataḥ
mahāyogaṃ mahātmānaṃ durdharṣam amarair api //
4.d:
ज्वलद्भिर् निशितैर् बाणैर् दीप्ततेजसम् अन्ततः
महायोगं महात्मानं दुर्धर्षम् अमरैर् अपि ॥
4.m: blazing with fierce splendor through his fiery, sharpened arrows, / possessed of great yoga, great-souled, invincible even by the immortals.

4.s:
alabhantī tu sā trāṇaṃ vaiṇyam evānvapadyata
kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā pūjyā lokais tribhis tadā //
4.d:
अलभन्ती तु सा त्राणं वैण्यम् एवान्वपद्यत
कृताञ्जलिपुटा भूत्वा पूज्या लोकैस् त्रिभिस् तदा ॥
4.m: Finding no protection, she surrendered to the son of Veṇa alone, / making an añjali gesture, though she was worthy of worship by the three worlds.

4.s:
uvāca vaiṇyaṃ nādharmaṃ strīvadhe paripaśyasi
kathaṃ dhārayitā cāsi prajā rājan vinā mayā //
4.d:
उवाच वैण्यं नाधर्मं स्त्रीवधे परिपश्यसि
कथं धारयिता चासि प्रजा राजन् विना मया ॥
4.m: She said to the son of Veṇa: "Do you not see unrighteousness in killing a woman? / And how will you sustain your subjects, O king, without me?

4.s:
mayi lokāḥ sthitā rājan mayedaṃ dhāryate jagat
madvināśe vinaśyeyuḥ prajāḥ pārthiva viddhi tat //
4.d:
मयि लोकाः स्थिता राजन् मयेदं धार्यते जगत्
मद्विनाशे विनश्येयुः प्रजाः पार्थिव विद्धि तत् ॥
4.m: In me the worlds are established, O king; by me this world is sustained; / upon my destruction the subjects would perish, O king—know this!

4.s:
na mām arhasi hantuṃ vai śreyaś cet tvaṃ cikīrṣasi
prajānāṃ pṛthivīpāla śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama //
4.d:
न माम् अर्हसि हन्तुं वै श्रेयश् चेत् त्वं चिकीर्षसि
प्रजानां पृथिवीपाल शृणु चेदं वचो मम ॥
4.m: You ought not to kill me if you wish to act for the welfare / of the subjects, O protector of the earth; listen to these words of mine.

4.s:
upāyataḥ samārabdhāḥ sarve sidhyanty upakramāḥ
upāyaṃ paśya yena tvaṃ dhārayethāḥ prajām imām //
4.d:
उपायतः समारब्धाः सर्वे सिध्यन्त्य् उपक्रमाः
उपायं पश्य येन त्वं धारयेथाः प्रजाम् इमाम् ॥
4.m: All undertakings begun with the proper means succeed; / look for a means by which you can sustain these subjects.

4.s:
hatvāpi māṃ na śaktas tvaṃ prajānāṃ poṣaṇe nṛpa
anukūlā bhaviṣyāmi yaccha kopaṃ mahāmate //
4.d:
हत्वापि मां न शक्तस् त्वं प्रजानां पोषणे नृप
अनुकूला भविष्यामि यच्छ कोपं महामते ॥
4.m: Even after killing me, you will not be able to nourish your subjects, O king; / I shall be compliant; restrain your anger, O high-minded one!

4.s:
avadhyāṃ ca striyaṃ prāhus tiryagyonigateṣv api
yady evaṃ pṛthivīpāla na dharmaṃ tyaktum arhasi //
4.d:
अवध्यां च स्त्रियं प्राहुस् तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्व् अपि
यद्य् एवं पृथिवीपाल न धर्मं त्यक्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
4.m: They declare that a female is not to be killed, even among animals; / since this is so, O protector of the earth, you ought not to abandon dharma."

4.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā rājā mahāmanāḥ
kopaṃ nigṛhya dharmātmā vasudhām idam abravīt //
4.d:
एवं बहुविधं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा राजा महामनाः
कोपं निगृह्य धर्मात्मा वसुधाम् इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥
4.m: Having heard this manifold speech, the high-minded, righteous king / restrained his anger and spoke thus to the earth:

4.s:
pṛthur uvāca
ekasyārthe tu yo hanyād ātmano vā parasya vā
bahūn vā prāṇino 'nantaṃ bhavet tasyeha pātakam //
4.d:
पृथुर् उवाच
एकस्यार्थे तु यो हन्याद् आत्मनो वा परस्य वा
बहून् वा प्राणिनो ऽनन्तं भवेत् तस्येह पातकम् ॥
4.m: Pṛthu said: / "He who kills many living beings for the sake of one, / whether for himself or for another, would incur endless sin in this world.

4.s:
sukham edhanti bahavo yasmiṃs tu nihate 'śubhe
tasmin hate nāsti bhadre pātakaṃ copapātakam //
4.d:
सुखम् एधन्ति बहवो यस्मिंस् तु निहते ऽशुभे
तस्मिन् हते नास्ति भद्रे पातकं चोपपातकम् ॥
4.m: However, when an inauspicious being is slain, if many prosper happily, / then upon the slaying of that one there is neither major sin nor minor sin, O auspicious one.

4.s:
so 'haṃ prajānimittaṃ tvāṃ haniṣyāmi vasuṃdhare
yadi me vacanān nādya kariṣyasi jagaddhitam //
4.d:
सो ऽहं प्रजानिमित्तं त्वां हनिष्यामि वसुंधरे
यदि मे वचनान् नाद्य करिष्यसि जगद्धितम् ॥
4.m: Therefore, for the sake of the subjects, I shall kill you, O Earth, / if you will not bring about the welfare of the world today according to my word.

4.s:
tvāṃ nihatyādya bāṇena macchāsanaparāṅmukhīm
ātmānaṃ prathayitvāhaṃ prajā dhārayitā svayam //
4.d:
त्वां निहत्याद्य बाणेन मच्छासनपराङ्मुखीम्
आत्मानं प्रथयित्वाहं प्रजा धारयिता स्वयम् ॥
4.m: Having struck you down today with an arrow because you turn away from my command, / I myself, having extended myself, shall sustain the subjects.

4.s:
sā tvaṃ śāsanam āsthāya mama dharmabhṛtāṃ vare
saṃjīvaya prajāḥ sarvāḥ samarthā hy asi dhāraṇe //
4.d:
सा त्वं शासनम् आस्थाय मम धर्मभृतां वरे
संजीवय प्रजाः सर्वाः समर्था ह्य् असि धारणे ॥
4.m: So, submitting to my command, O best among upholders of dharma, / give life to all the subjects, for you are indeed capable of sustaining [them].

4.s:
duhitṛtvaṃ ca me gaccha tata enam ahaṃ śaram
niyaccheyaṃ tvadvadhārtham udyantaṃ ghoradarśanam //
4.d:
दुहितृत्वं च मे गच्छ तत एनम् अहं शरम्
नियच्छेयं त्वद्वधार्थम् उद्यन्तं घोरदर्शनम् ॥
4.m: And become my daughter; then I shall withdraw this arrow of terrible appearance, / which is raised for your destruction."

4.s:
vasudhovāca
sarvam etad ahaṃ vīra vidhāsyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
vatsaṃ tu mama saṃpaśya kṣareyaṃ yena vatsalā //
4.d:
वसुधोवाच
सर्वम् एतद् अहं वीर विधास्यामि न संशयः
वत्सं तु मम संपश्य क्षरेयं येन वत्सला ॥

4.s:
samāṃ ca kuru sarvatra māṃ tvaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
yathā visyandamānaṃ me kṣīraṃ sarvatra bhāvayet //
4.d:
समां च कुरु सर्वत्र मां त्वं धर्मभृतां वर
यथा विस्यन्दमानं मे क्षीरं सर्वत्र भावयेत् ॥
4.m:
And make me level everywhere, O best of upholders of dharma,
so that my trickling milk may foster everything everywhere.”

4.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
tata utsārayām āsa śailāñ śatasahasraśaḥ
dhanuṣkoṭyā tadā vaiṇyas tena śailā vivardhitāḥ //
4.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
तत उत्सारयाम् आस शैलाञ् शतसहस्रशः
धनुष्कोट्या तदा वैण्यस् तेन शैला विवर्धिताः ॥
4.m:
Lomaharṣaṇa said:
Then the son of Vena cleared away the mountains by hundreds of thousands
with the tip of his bow; thus the mountains were piled up.

4.s:
nahi pūrvavisarge vai viṣame pṛthivītale
saṃvibhāgaḥ purāṇāṃ vā grāmāṇāṃ vābhavat tadā //
4.d:
नहि पूर्वविसर्गे वै विषमे पृथिवीतले
संविभागः पुराणां वा ग्रामाणां वाभवत् तदा ॥
4.m:
Indeed, in the previous creation, upon the uneven surface of the earth,
there was then no division into cities or villages,

4.s:
na sasyāni na gorakṣyaṃ na kṛṣir na vaṇikpathaḥ
naiva satyānṛtaṃ cāsīn na lobho na ca matsaraḥ //
4.d:
न सस्यानि न गोरक्ष्यं न कृषिर् न वणिक्पथः
नैव सत्यानृतं चासीन् न लोभो न च मत्सरः ॥
4.m:
no crops, no cattle-rearing, no agriculture, no trade-route;
there was neither truth nor falsehood, neither greed nor malice.

4.s:
vaivasvate 'ntare tasmin sāṃprataṃ samupasthite
vaiṇyāt prabhṛti vai viprāḥ sarvasyaitasya saṃbhavaḥ //
4.d:
वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे तस्मिन् सांप्रतं समुपस्थिते
वैण्यात् प्रभृति वै विप्राः सर्वस्यैतस्य संभवः ॥
4.m:
When that Vaivasvata interval arrived at the present time,
O twice-born, the origin of all this began from the son of Vena.

4.s:
yatra yatra samaṃ tv asyā bhūmer āsīt tadā dvijāḥ
tatra tatra prajāḥ sarvā nivāsaṃ samarocayan //
4.d:
यत्र यत्र समं त्व् अस्या भूमेर् आसीत् तदा द्विजाः
तत्र तत्र प्रजाः सर्वा निवासं समरोचयन् ॥
4.m:
Wherever this earth was level at that time, O twice-born,
there all the creatures chose to settle.

4.s:
āhāraḥ phalamūlāni prajānām abhavat tadā
kṛcchreṇa mahatā yukta ity evam anuśuśruma //
4.d:
आहारः फलमूलानि प्रजानाम् अभवत् तदा
कृच्छ्रेण महता युक्त इत्य् एवम् अनुशुश्रुम ॥
4.m:
Fruits and roots were then the food of the creatures,
attended with great hardship—thus we have heard.

4.s:
sa kalpayitvā vatsaṃ tu manuṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ prabhum
svapāṇau puruṣavyāghro dudoha pṛthivīṃ tataḥ //
4.d:
स कल्पयित्वा वत्सं तु मनुं स्वायंभुवं प्रभुम्
स्वपाणौ पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुदोह पृथिवीं ततः ॥
4.m:
Having made the lord Manu Svāyambhuva the calf,
that tiger among men milked the earth into his own hand.

4.s:
sasyajātāni sarvāṇi pṛthur vaiṇyaḥ pratāpavān
tenānnena prajāḥ sarvā vartante 'dyāpi sarvaśaḥ //
4.d:
सस्यजातानि सर्वाणि पृथुर् वैण्यः प्रतापवान्
तेनान्नेन प्रजाः सर्वा वर्तन्ते ऽद्यापि सर्वशः ॥
4.m:
The majestic Pṛthu, son of Vena, [milked] all the kinds of crops;
by that food all the creatures subsist everywhere even today.

4.s:
ṛṣayaś ca tadā devāḥ pitaro 'tha sarīsṛpāḥ
daityā yakṣāḥ puṇyajanā gandharvāḥ parvatā nagāḥ //
4.d:
ऋषयश् च तदा देवाः पितरो ऽथ सरीसृपाः
दैत्या यक्षाः पुण्यजना गन्धर्वाः पर्वता नगाः ॥
4.m:
Then the sages, the gods, the ancestors, the serpents,
the daityas, the yakṣas, the puṇyajanas, the gandharvas, the mountains, and the trees—

4.s:
ete purā dvijaśreṣṭhā duduhur dharaṇīṃ kila
kṣīraṃ vatsaś ca pātraṃ ca teṣāṃ dogdhā pṛthak pṛthak //
4.d:
एते पुरा द्विजश्रेष्ठा दुदुहुर् धरणीं किल
क्षीरं वत्सश् च पात्रं च तेषां दोग्धा पृथक् पृथक् ॥
4.m:
all these, O best of twice-born, milked the earth in ancient times,
each with their own distinct milk, calf, vessel, and milker.

4.s:
ṛṣīṇām abhavat somo vatso dogdhā bṛhaspatiḥ
kṣīraṃ teṣāṃ tapo brahma pātraṃ chandāṃsi bho dvijāḥ //
4.d:
ऋषीणाम् अभवत् सोमो वत्सो दोग्धा बृहस्पतिः
क्षीरं तेषां तपो ब्रह्म पात्रं छन्दांसि भो द्विजाः ॥
4.m:
Soma was the calf of the sages, and Bṛhaspati the milker;
their milk was austerity and brahma, and the metres were the vessel, O twice-born.

4.s:
devānāṃ kāñcanaṃ pātraṃ vatsas teṣāṃ śatakratuḥ
kṣīram ojaskaraṃ caiva dogdhā ca bhagavān raviḥ //
4.d:
देवानां काञ्चनं पात्रं वत्सस् तेषां शतक्रतुः
क्षीरम् ओजस्करं चैव दोग्धा च भगवान् रविः ॥
4.m:
The vessel of the gods was of gold, Śatakratu was their calf,
the milk was vigor-giving, and the milker was the blessed Sun.

4.s:
pitṝṇāṃ rājataṃ pātraṃ yamo vatsaḥ pratāpavān
antakaś cābhavad dogdhā kṣīraṃ teṣāṃ sudhā smṛtā //
4.d:
पितॄणां राजतं पात्रं यमो वत्सः प्रतापवान्
अन्तकश् चाभवद् दोग्धा क्षीरं तेषां सुधा स्मृता ॥
4.m:
The vessel of the ancestors was of silver, the mighty Yama was the calf,
Antaka was the milker, and their milk is declared to be nectar.

4.s:
nāgānāṃ takṣako vatsaḥ pātraṃ cālābusaṃjñakam
dogdhā tv airāvato nāgas teṣāṃ kṣīraṃ viṣaṃ smṛtam //
4.d:
नागानां तक्षको वत्सः पात्रं चालाबुसंज्ञकम्
दोग्धा त्व् ऐरावतो नागस् तेषां क्षीरं विषं स्मृतम् ॥
4.m:
Takṣaka was the calf of the serpents, and the vessel was called a gourd;
the elephant Airāvata was the milker, and their milk is declared to be poison.

4.s:
asurāṇāṃ madhur dogdhā kṣīraṃ māyāmayaṃ smṛtam
virocanas tu vatso 'bhūd āyasaṃ pātram eva ca //
4.d:
असुराणां मधुर् दोग्धा क्षीरं मायामयं स्मृतम्
विरोचनस् तु वत्सो ऽभूद् आयसं पात्रम् एव च ॥
4.m:
Madhu was the milker of the asuras, the milk is declared to be of illusory power,
Virocana was the calf, and the vessel was made of iron.

4.s:
yakṣāṇām āmapātraṃ tu vatso vaiśravaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
dogdhā rajatanābhas tu kṣīrāntardhānam eva ca //
4.d:
यक्षाणाम् आमपात्रं तु वत्सो वैश्रवणः प्रभुः
दोग्धा रजतनाभस् तु क्षीरान्तर्धानम् एव च ॥
4.m:
The vessel of the yakṣas was unbaked clay, the lord Vaiśravaṇa the calf,
Rajatanābha the milker, and their milk was disappearance.

4.s:
sumālī rākṣasendrāṇāṃ vatsaḥ kṣīraṃ ca śoṇitam
dogdhā rajatanābhas tu kapālaṃ pātram eva ca //
4.d:
सुमाली राक्षसेन्द्राणां वत्सः क्षीरं च शोणितम्
दोग्धा रजतनाभस् तु कपालं पात्रम् एव च ॥
4.m:
Sumālī was the calf of the rakṣasa chiefs, and blood was the milk;
Rajatanābha was the milker, and a skull was the vessel.

4.s:
gandharvāṇāṃ citraratho vatsaḥ pātraṃ ca paṅkajam
dogdhā ca suruciḥ kṣīraṃ teṣāṃ gandhaḥ śuciḥ smṛtaḥ //
4.d:
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथो वत्सः पात्रं च पङ्कजम्
दोग्धा च सुरुचिः क्षीरं तेषां गन्धः शुचिः स्मृतः ॥
4.m:
Citraratha was the calf of the gandharvas, and a lotus was the vessel;
Suruci was the milker, and their milk is declared to be pure fragrance.

4.s:
śailaṃ pātraṃ parvatānāṃ kṣīraṃ ratnauṣadhīs tathā
vatsas tu himavān āsīd dogdhā merur mahāgiriḥ //
4.d:
शैलं पात्रं पर्वतानां क्षीरं रत्नौषधीस् तथा
वत्सस् तु हिमवान् आसीद् दोग्धा मेरुर् महागिरिः ॥
4.m:
The vessel of the mountains was of stone, and the milk was gems and herbs;
Himavat was the calf, and the great mountain Meru was the milker.

4.s:
plakṣo vatsas tu vṛkṣāṇāṃ dogdhā śālas tu puṣpitaḥ
pālāśapātraṃ kṣīraṃ ca cchinnadagdhaprarohaṇam //
4.d:
प्लक्षो वत्सस् तु वृक्षाणां दोग्धा शालस् तु पुष्पितः
पालाशपात्रं क्षीरं च च्छिन्नदग्धप्ररोहणम् ॥
4.m:
The plakṣa tree was the calf of the trees, and the flowering śāla was the milker;
the vessel was of palāśa wood, and the milk was regrowth when cut or burnt.

4.s:
seyaṃ dhātrī vidhātrī ca pāvanī ca vasuṃdharā
carācarasya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā yonir eva ca //
4.d:
सेयं धात्री विधात्री च पावनी च वसुंधरा
चराचरस्य सर्वस्य प्रतिष्ठा योनिर् एव च ॥
4.m:
She is the supporter, the ordainer, the purifier, the bearer of wealth,
the foundation and the source of everything moving and unmoving.

4.s:
sarvakāmadughā dogdhrī sarvasasyaprarohaṇī
āsīd iyaṃ samudrāntā medinī pariviśrutā //
4.d:
सर्वकामदुघा दोग्ध्री सर्वसस्यप्ररोहणी
आसीद् इयं समुद्रान्ता मेदिनी परिविश्रुता ॥
4.m:
She is the milch-cow yielding all desires, the milker, the sprouter of all crops;
this earth, bounded by the ocean, became widely renowned.

4.s:
madhukaiṭabhayoḥ kṛtsnā medasā samabhiplutā
teneyaṃ medinī devī ucyate brahmavādibhiḥ //
4.d:
मधुकैटभयोः कृत्स्ना मेदसा समभिप्लुता
तेनेयं मेदिनी देवी उच्यते ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥
4.m:
She was completely drenched with the fat of Madhu and Kaiṭabha;
therefore is this goddess called Medinī by the expounders of the Veda.

4.s:
tato 'bhyupagamād rājñaḥ pṛthor vaiṇyasya bho dvijāḥ
duhitṛtvam anuprāptā devī pṛthvīti cocyate //
4.d:
ततो ऽभ्युपगमाद् राज्ञः पृथोर् वैण्यस्य भो द्विजाः
दुहितृत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता देवी पृथ्वीति चोच्यते ॥
4.m:
Then, from the acceptance by King Pṛthu, the son of Vena, O twice-born,
the goddess attained daughterhood and is also called Pṛthvī.

4.s:
pṛthunā pravibhaktā ca śodhitā ca vasuṃdharā
sasyākaravatī sphītā purapattanaśālinī //
4.d:
पृथुना प्रविभक्ता च शोधिता च वसुंधरा
सस्याकरवती स्फीता पुरपत्तनशालिनी ॥
4.m:
The earth was parcelled out and cleared by Pṛthu,
made rich with crops and mines, and adorned with cities and towns.

4.s:
evaṃprabhāvo vaiṇyaḥ sa rājāsīd rājasattamaḥ
namasyaś caiva pūjyaś ca bhūtagrāmair na saṃśayaḥ //
4.d:
एवंप्रभावो वैण्यः स राजासीद् राजसत्तमः
नमस्यश् चैव पूज्यश् च भूतग्रामैर् न संशयः ॥
4.m:
Such was the power of that king, the son of Vena, the best of kings;
he is to be bowed to and worshipped by all beings, there is no doubt.

4.s:
brāhmaṇaiś ca mahābhāgair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ
pṛthur eva namaskāryo brahmayoniḥ sanātanaḥ //
4.d:
ब्राह्मणैश् च महाभागैर् वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः
पृथुर् एव नमस्कार्यो ब्रह्मयोनिः सनातनः ॥
4.m:
By illustrious brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
Pṛthu alone is to be saluted, the eternal source of brahma.

4.s:
pārthivaiś ca mahābhāgaiḥ pārthivatvam ihecchubhiḥ
ādirājo namaskāryaḥ pṛthur vaiṇyaḥ pratāpavān //
4.d:
पार्थिवैश् च महाभागैः पार्थिवत्वम् इहेच्छुभिः
आदिराजो नमस्कार्यः पृथुर् वैण्यः प्रतापवान् ॥
4.m:
And by illustrious earthly kings desiring sovereignty here on earth,
the first king is to be saluted, the majestic Pṛthu, son of Vena.

4.s:
yodhair api ca vikrāntaiḥ prāptukāmair jayaṃ yudhi
ādirājo namaskāryo yodhānāṃ prathamo nṛpaḥ //
4.d:
योधैर् अपि च विक्रान्तैः प्राप्तुकामैर् जयं युधि
आदिराजो नमस्कार्यो योधानां प्रथमो नृपः ॥
4.m:
Even by valiant warriors desiring to attain victory in battle,
the first king is to be saluted, the first king among warriors.

4.s:
yo hi yoddhā raṇaṃ yāti kīrtayitvā pṛthuṃ nṛpam
sa ghorarūpāt saṃgrāmāt kṣemī bhavati kīrtimān //
4.d:
यो हि योद्धा रणं याति कीर्तयित्वा पृथुं नृपम्
स घोररूपात् संग्रामात् क्षेमी भवति कीर्तिमान् ॥
4.m:
For whatever warrior goes to battle having praised King Pṛthu,
he comes safely out of terrible battle, full of renown.

4.s:
vaiśyair api ca vittāḍhyair vaiśyavṛttividhāyibhiḥ
pṛthur eva namaskāryo vṛttidātā mahāyaśāḥ //
4.d:
वैश्यैर् अपि च वित्ताढ्यैर् वैश्यवृत्तिविधायिभिः
पृथुर् एव नमस्कार्यो वृत्तिदाता महायशाः ॥
4.m:
By vaiśyas too, rich in wealth and following the vocation of a vaiśya,
Pṛthu alone is to be saluted, the giver of livelihood, of great renown.

4.s:
tathaiva śūdraiḥ śucibhis trivarṇaparicāribhiḥ
pṛthur eva namaskāryaḥ śreyaḥ param ihepsubhiḥ //
4.d:
तथैव शूद्रैः शुचिभिस् त्रिवर्णपरिचारिभिः
पृथुर् एव नमस्कार्यः श्रेयः परम् इहेप्सुभिः ॥
4.m:
Likewise, by pure śūdras who serve the three castes
and desire supreme welfare here, Pṛthu alone is to be saluted.

4.s:
ete vatsaviśeṣāś ca dogdhāraḥ kṣīram eva ca
pātrāṇi ca mayoktāni kiṃ bhūyo varṇayāmi vaḥ //
4.d:
एते वत्सविशेषाश् च दोग्धारः क्षीरम् एव च
पात्राणि च मयोक्तानि किं भूयो वर्णयामि वः ॥
4.m:
These various calves, milkers, kinds of milk,
and vessels have been related by me. What more shall I describe to you?

5.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
manvantarāṇi sarvāṇi vistareṇa mahāmate
teṣāṃ pūrvavisṛṣṭiṃ ca lomaharṣaṇa kīrtaya //
5.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
मन्वन्तराणि सर्वाणि विस्तरेण महामते
तेषां पूर्वविसृष्टिं च लोमहर्षण कीर्तय ॥
5.m:
The sages said:
Declare in detail all the manvantaras, O high-minded one,
and their previous creations, O Lomaharṣaṇa.

5.s:
yāvanto manavaś caiva yāvantaṃ kālam eva ca
manvantarāṇi bhoḥ sūta śrotum icchāma tattvataḥ //
5.d:
यावन्तो मनवश् चैव यावन्तं कालम् एव च
मन्वन्तराणि भोः सूत श्रोतुम् इच्छाम तत्त्वतः ॥
5.m:
How many Manus there are, and for how long a time—
we wish to hear the manvantaras in truth, O bard.

5.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
na śakyo vistaro viprā vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api
manvantarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃkṣepāc chṛṇuta dvijāḥ //
5.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
न शक्यो विस्तरो विप्रा वक्तुं वर्षशतैर् अपि
मन्वन्तराणां सर्वेषां संक्षेपाच् छृणुत द्विजाः ॥

5.s:
svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ pūrvaṃ manuḥ svārociṣas tathā
uttamas tāmasaś caiva raivataś cākṣuṣas tathā //
5.d:
स्वायंभुवो मनुः पूर्वं मनुः स्वारोचिषस् तथा
उत्तमस् तामसश् चैव रैवतश् चाक्षुषस् तथा ॥
5.m:
Svāyambhuva was the first Manu, then Manu Svārociṣa,
Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa;

5.s:
vaivasvataś ca bho viprāḥ sāṃprataṃ manur ucyate
sāvarṇiś ca manus tadvad raibhyo raucyas tathaiva ca //
5.d:
वैवस्वतश् च भो विप्राः सांप्रतं मनुर् उच्यते
सावर्णिश् च मनुस् तद्वद् रैभ्यो रौच्यस् तथैव च ॥
5.m:
and Vaivasvata, O twice-born, is called the present Manu;
likewise Sāvarṇi Manu, and Raibhya, and Raucya;

5.s:
tathaiva merusāvarṇyaś catvāro manavaḥ smṛtāḥ
atītā vartamānāś ca tathaivānāgatā dvijāḥ //
5.d:
तथैव मेरुसावर्ण्यश् चत्वारो मनवः स्मृताः
अतीता वर्तमानाश् च तथैवानागता द्विजाः ॥
5.m:
and likewise four Merusāvarṇya Manus are remembered—
past, present, and future, O twice-born.

5.s:
kīrtitā manavas tubhyaṃ mayaivaite yathā śrutāḥ
ṛṣīṃs tv eṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi putrān devagaṇāṃs tathā //
5.d:
कीर्तिता मनवस् तुभ्यं मयैवैते यथा श्रुताः
ऋषींस् त्व् एषां प्रवक्ष्यामि पुत्रान् देवगणांस् तथा ॥
5.m:
These Manus have been proclaimed to you by me just as I heard them;
now I shall declare their sages, sons, and the hosts of gods.

5.s:
marīcir atrir bhagavān aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
pulastyaś ca vasiṣṭhaś ca saptaite brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ //
5.d:
मरीचिर् अत्रिर् भगवान् अङ्गिराः पुलहः क्रतुः
पुलस्त्यश् च वसिष्ठश् च सप्तैते ब्रह्मणः सुताः ॥
5.m:
Marīci, the blessed Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu,
Pulastya, and Vasiṣṭha—these are the seven sons of Brahmā,

5.s:
uttarasyāṃ diśi tathā dvijāḥ saptarṣayas tathā
āgniidhraś cāgnibāhuś ca medhyo medhātithir vasuḥ //
5.d:
उत्तरस्यां दिशि तथा द्विजाः सप्तर्षयस् तथा
आग्निइध्रश् चाग्निबाहुश् च मेध्यो मेधातिथिर् वसुः ॥
5.m:
the seven sages in the northern direction, O twice-born.
Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Medhya, Medhātithi, Vasu,

5.s:
jyotiṣmān dyutimān havyaḥ savalaḥ putrasaṃjñakaḥ
manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasyaite daśa putrā mahaujasaḥ //
5.d:
ज्योतिष्मान् द्युतिमान् हव्यः सवलः पुत्रसंज्ञकः
मनोः स्वायंभुवस्यैते दश पुत्रा महौजसः ॥
5.m:
Jyotiṣmat, Dyutimat, Havya, Savala, and one named Putra—
these are the ten highly energetic sons of Manu Svāyambhuva.

5.s:
etad vai prathamaṃ viprā manvantaram udāhṛtam
aurvo vasiṣṭhaputraś ca stambaḥ kaśyapa eva ca //
5.d:
एतद् वै प्रथमं विप्रा मन्वन्तरम् उदाहृतम्
और्वो वसिष्ठपुत्रश् च स्तम्बः कश्यप एव च ॥
5.m:
This is declared to be the first manvantara, O twice-born.
Aurva, the son of Vasiṣṭha, Stamba, and Kaśyapa,

5.s:
prāṇo bṛhaspatiś caiva datto 'triccyavanas tathā
ete maharṣayo viprā vāyuproktā mahāvratāḥ //
5.d:
प्राणो बृहस्पतिश् चैव दत्तो ऽत्रिच्च्यवनस् तथा
एते महर्षयो विप्रा वायुप्रोक्ता महाव्रताः ॥
5.m: Prāṇa, Bṛhaspati, Datta, the descendant of Atri, and Cyavana— / these, O twice-born, are the great sages of mighty vows proclaimed by Vāyu.

5.s:
devāś ca tuṣitā nāma smṛtāḥ svārociṣe 'ntare
havighnaḥ sukṛtir jyotir āpo mūrtir api smṛtaḥ //
5.d:
देवाश् च तुषिता नाम स्मृताः स्वारोचिषे ऽन्तरे
हविघ्नः सुकृतिर् ज्योतिर् आपो मूर्तिर् अपि स्मृतः ॥
5.m: And the gods in the Svārociṣa period are remembered as the Tuṣitas. / Havighna, Sukṛti, Jyotis, Āpas, and Mūrti are recorded,

5.s:
pratītaś ca nabhasyaś ca nabha ūrjas tathaiva ca
svārociṣasya putrās te manor viprā mahātmanaḥ //
5.d:
प्रतीतश् च नभस्यश् च नभ ऊर्जस् तथैव च
स्वारोचिषस्य पुत्रास् ते मनोर् विप्रा महात्मनः ॥
5.m: and Pratīta, Nabhasya, Nabha, and Ūrja likewise— / these, O twice-born, are the sons of the great-souled Svārociṣa Manu,

5.s:
kīrtitāḥ pṛthivīpālā mahāvīryaparākramāḥ
dvitīyam etat kathitaṃ viprā manvantaraṃ mayā //
5.d:
कीर्तिताः पृथिवीपाला महावीर्यपराक्रमाः
द्वितीयम् एतत् कथितं विप्रा मन्वन्तरं मया ॥
5.m: celebrated as earth-protectors of great power and valour. / This second manvantara has been related by me, O twice-born.

5.s:
idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vakṣyāmi tad budhyadhvaṃ dvijottamāḥ
vasiṣṭhaputrāḥ saptāsan vāsiṣṭhā iti viśrutāḥ //
5.d:
इदं तृतीयं वक्ष्यामि तद् बुध्यध्वं द्विजोत्तमाः
वसिष्ठपुत्राः सप्तासन् वासिष्ठा इति विश्रुताः ॥
5.m: I shall speak of this third one; understand it, O best of twice-born: / there were seven sons of Vasiṣṭha renowned as the Vāsiṣṭhas.

5.s:
hiraṇyagarbhasya sutā ūrjā jātāḥ sutejasaḥ
ṛṣayo 'tra mayā proktāḥ kīrtyamānān nibodhata //
5.d:
हिरण्यगर्भस्य सुता ऊर्जा जाताः सुतेजसः
ऋषयो ऽत्र मया प्रोक्ताः कीर्त्यमानान् निबोधत ॥
5.m: Sons of Hiraṇyagarbha, born of Ūrjā, possessing great splendor— / these sages here have been declared by me; listen to them as they are proclaimed.

5.s:
auttameyān muniśreṣṭhā daśa putrān manor imān
iṣa ūrjas tanūrjas tu madhur mādhava eva ca //
5.d:
औत्तमेयान् मुनिश्रेष्ठा दश पुत्रान् मनोर् इमान्
इष ऊर्जस् तनूर्जस् तु मधुर् माधव एव च ॥
5.m: These are the ten sons of Manu Auttami, O best of sages: / Iṣa, Ūrja, Tanūrja, Madhu, and Mādhava,

5.s:
śuciḥ śukraḥ sahaś caiva nabhasyo nabha eva ca
bhānavas tatra devāś ca manvantaram udāhṛtam //
5.d:
शुचिः शुक्रः सहश् चैव नभस्यो नभ एव च
भानवस् तत्र देवाश् च मन्वन्तरम् उदाहृतम् ॥
5.m: Śuci, Śukra, Saha, Nabhasya, and Nabha. / The gods there were the Bhānavas; thus is the manvantara described.

5.s:
manvantaraṃ caturthaṃ vaḥ kathayiṣyāmi sāṃpratam
kāvyaḥ pṛthus tathaivāgnir jahnur dhātā dvijottamāḥ //
5.d:
मन्वन्तरं चतुर्थं वः कथयिष्यामि सांप्रतम्
काव्यः पृथुस् तथैवाग्निर् जह्नुर् धाता द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
5.m: I will now tell you the fourth manvantara, O best of twice-born: / Kāvya, Pṛthu, Agni, Jahnu, Dhātṛ,

5.s:
kapīvān akapīvāṃś ca tatra saptarṣayo dvijāḥ
purāṇe kīrtitā viprāḥ putrāḥ pautrāś ca bho dvijāḥ //
5.d:
कपीवान् अकपीवांश् च तत्र सप्तर्षयो द्विजाः
पुराणे कीर्तिता विप्राः पुत्राः पौत्राश् च भो द्विजाः ॥
5.m: Kapīvat, and Akapīvat—there these are the seven sages, O twice-born; / their sons and grandsons are celebrated in the Purāṇa, O twice-born.

5.s:
tathā devagaṇāś caiva tāmasasyāntare manoḥ
dyutis tapasyaḥ sutapās tapobhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ //
5.d:
तथा देवगणाश् चैव तामसस्यान्तरे मनोः
द्युतिस् तपस्यः सुतपास् तपोभूतः सनातनः ॥
5.m: Likewise are the groups of gods in the period of Tāmasa Manu: / Dyuti, Tapasya, Sutapas, Tapobhūta, Sanātana,

5.s:
taporatir akalmāṣas tanvī dhanvī paraṃtapaḥ
tāmasasya manor ete daśa putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
5.d:
तपोरतिर् अकल्माषस् तन्वी धन्वी परंतपः
तामसस्य मनोर् एते दश पुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
5.m: Taporati, Akalmāṣa, Tanvī, Dhanvī, and Paraṃtapa— / these ten are proclaimed as the sons of Tāmasa Manu.

5.s:
vāyuproktā muniśreṣṭhāś caturthaṃ caitad antaram
devabāhur yadudhraś ca munir vedaśirās tathā //
5.d:
वायुप्रोक्ता मुनिश्रेष्ठाश् चतुर्थं चैतद् अन्तरम्
देवबाहुर् यदुध्रश् च मुनिर् वेदशिरास् तथा ॥
5.m: These best of sages were proclaimed by Vāyu; and this is the fourth period. / Devabāhu, Yadudhra, and the sage Vedaśiras,

5.s:
hiraṇyaromā parjanya ūrdhvabāhuś ca somajaḥ
satyanetras tathātreya ete saptarṣayo 'pare //
5.d:
हिरण्यरोमा पर्जन्य ऊर्ध्वबाहुश् च सोमजः
सत्यनेत्रस् तथात्रेय एते सप्तर्षयो ऽपरे ॥
5.m: Hiraṇyaroman, Parjanya, Ūrdhvabāhu born of Soma, / and Satyanetra descendant of Atri—these other seven are the seven sages.

5.s:
devāś cābhūtarajasas tathā prakṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ
vāriplavaś ca raibhyaś ca manor antaram ucyate //
5.d:
देवाश् चाभूतरजसस् तथा प्रकृतयः स्मृताः
वारिप्लवश् च रैभ्यश् च मनोर् अन्तरम् उच्यते ॥
5.m: The gods are remembered as the Abhūtarajases and the Prakṛtis. / The period of Manu Vāriplava Raibhya is now recounted:

5.s:
atha putrān imāṃs tasya budhyadhvaṃ gadato mama
dhṛtimān avyayo yuktas tattvadarśī nirutsukaḥ //
5.d:
अथ पुत्रान् इमांस् तस्य बुध्यध्वं गदतो मम
धृतिमान् अव्ययो युक्तस् तत्त्वदर्शी निरुत्सुकः ॥
5.m: Hear now from me, as I speak, these sons of his: / Dhṛtimat, Avyaya, Yukta, Tattvadarśin, Nirutsuka,

5.s:
āraṇyaś ca prakāśaś ca nirmohaḥ satyavāk kṛtī
raivatasya manoḥ putrāḥ pañcamaṃ caitad antaram //
5.d:
आरण्यश् च प्रकाशश् च निर्मोहः सत्यवाक् कृती
रैवतस्य मनोः पुत्राः पञ्चमं चैतद् अन्तरम् ॥
5.m: Āraṇya, Prakāśa, Nirmoha, Satyavāc, and Kṛtin— / these are the sons of Raivata Manu, and this is the fifth period.

5.s:
ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu saṃpravakṣyāmi tad budhyadhvaṃ dvijottamāḥ
bhṛgur nabho vivasvāṃś ca sudhāmā virajās tathā //
5.d:
षष्ठं तु संप्रवक्ष्यामि तद् बुध्यध्वं द्विजोत्तमाः
भृगुर् नभो विवस्वांश् च सुधामा विरजास् तथा ॥
5.m: Now I shall proclaim the sixth; understand it, O best of twice-born: / Bhṛgu, Nabha, Vivasvat, Sudhāman, Virajas,

5.s:
atināmā sahiṣṇuś ca saptaite ca maharṣayaḥ
cākṣuṣasyāntare viprā manor devās tv ime smṛtāḥ //
5.d:
अतिनामा सहिष्णुश् च सप्तैते च महर्षयः
चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे विप्रा मनोर् देवास् त्व् इमे स्मृताः ॥
5.m: Atināman, and Sahiṣṇu—these seven are the great sages / in the period of Cākṣuṣa Manu, O twice-born, and these are remembered as the gods:

5.s:
ābālaprathitās te vai pṛthaktvena divaukasaḥ
lekhāś ca nāmato viprāḥ pañca devagaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
5.d:
आबालप्रथितास् ते वै पृथक्त्वेन दिवौकसः
लेखाश् च नामतो विप्राः पञ्च देवगणाः स्मृताः ॥
5.m: Those denizens of heaven are renowned individually from youth up; / by name they are the Lekhas, O twice-born, remembered as five groups of gods.

5.s:
ṛṣer aṅgirasaḥ putrā mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ
nāḍvaleyā muniśreṣṭhā daśa putrās tu viśrutāḥ //
5.d:
ऋषेर् अङ्गिरसः पुत्रा महात्मानो महौजसः
नाड्वलेया मुनिश्रेष्ठा दश पुत्रास् तु विश्रुताः ॥
5.m: The sons of the sage Aṅgiras were great-souled and of mighty vigor. / The sons of Naḍvalā, O best of sages, are renowned as ten sons,

5.s:
ruruprabhṛtayo viprāś cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ
ṣaṣṭhaṃ manvantaraṃ proktaṃ saptamaṃ tu nibodhata //
5.d:
रुरुप्रभृतयो विप्राश् चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः
षष्ठं मन्वन्तरं प्रोक्तं सप्तमं तु निबोधत ॥
5.m: Ruru and others, O twice-born, in the period of Cākṣuṣa Manu. / The sixth manvantara has been declared; now learn of the seventh:

5.s:
atrir vasiṣṭho bhagavān kaśyapaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ
gautamo 'tha bharadvājo viśvāmitras tathaiva ca //
5.d:
अत्रिर् वसिष्ठो भगवान् कश्यपश् च महान् ऋषिः
गौतमो ऽथ भरद्वाजो विश्वामित्रस् तथैव च ॥
5.m: Atri, the lord Vasiṣṭha, and Kaśyapa the great sage, / Gautama, then Bharadvāja, and likewise Viśvāmitra,

5.s:
tathaiva putro bhagavān ṛcīkasya mahātmanaḥ
saptamo jamadagniś ca ṛṣayaḥ sāṃprataṃ divi //
5.d:
तथैव पुत्रो भगवान् ऋचीकस्य महात्मनः
सप्तमो जमदग्निश् च ऋषयः सांप्रतं दिवि ॥
5.m: and the seventh is the blessed Jamadagni, / the son of the great-souled Ṛcīka—these are the sages now in heaven.

5.s:
sādhyā rudrāś ca viśve ca vasavo marutas tathā
ādityāś cāśvinau cāpi devau vaivasvatau smṛtau //
5.d:
साध्या रुद्राश् च विश्वे च वसवो मरुतस् तथा
आदित्याश् चाश्विनौ चापि देवौ वैवस्वतौ स्मृतौ ॥
5.m: The Sādhyas, the Rudras, the Viśvedevas, the Vasus, the Maruts, / the Ādityas, and the two Aśvins are remembered as the gods of Vaivasvata.

5.s:
manor vaivasvatasyaite vartante sāṃprate 'ntare
ikṣvākupramukhāś caiva daśa putrā mahātmanaḥ //
5.d:
मनोर् वैवस्वतस्यैते वर्तन्ते सांप्रते ऽन्तरे
इक्ष्वाकुप्रमुखाश् चैव दश पुत्रा महात्मनः ॥
5.m: These abide in the present period of Vaivasvata Manu; / and there are ten sons of the great-souled one, led by Ikṣvāku.

5.s:
eteṣāṃ kīrtitānāṃ tu maharṣīṇāṃ mahaujasām
teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca dikṣu sarvāsu bho dvijāḥ //
5.d:
एतेषां कीर्तितानां तु महर्षीणां महौजसाम्
तेषां पुत्राश् च पौत्राश् च दिक्षु सर्वासु भो द्विजाः ॥
5.m: Of these proclaimed great sages of mighty vigor, / their sons and grandsons exist in all directions, O twice-born.

5.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu prāg āsan sapta saptakāḥ
loke dharmavyavasthārthaṃ lokasaṃrakṣaṇāya ca //
5.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु प्राग् आसन् सप्त सप्तकाः
लोके धर्मव्यवस्थार्थं लोकसंरक्षणाय च ॥
5.m: In all manvantaras there were previously seven sevens [of sages], / for the establishment of dharma in the world and for the protection of the worlds.

5.s:
manvantare vyatikrānte catvāraḥ saptakā gaṇāḥ
kṛtvā karma divaṃ yānti brahmalokam anāmayam //
5.d:
मन्वन्तरे व्यतिक्रान्ते चत्वारः सप्तका गणाः
कृत्वा कर्म दिवं यान्ति ब्रह्मलोकम् अनामयम् ॥
5.m: When a manvantara has elapsed, the four groups of seven, / having performed their work, go to heaven, to the disease-free world of Brahmā.

5.s:
tato 'nye tapasā yuktāḥ sthānaṃ tat pūrayanty uta
atītā vartamānāś ca krameṇaitena bho dvijāḥ //
5.d:
ततो ऽन्ये तपसा युक्ताः स्थानं तत् पूरयन्त्य् उत
अतीता वर्तमानाश् च क्रमेणैतेन भो द्विजाः ॥
5.m: Then others endowed with ascetic heat fill that post; / in this succession, O twice-born, past, present,

5.s:
anāgatāś ca saptaite smṛtā divi maharṣayaḥ
manor antaram āsādya sāvarṇasyeha bho dvijāḥ //
5.d:
अनागताश् च सप्तैते स्मृता दिवि महर्षयः
मनोर् अन्तरम् आसाद्य सावर्णस्येह भो द्विजाः ॥
5.m: and future—these seven great sages are remembered in heaven. / Arriving at the period of Sāvarṇa Manu here, O twice-born,

5.s:
rāmo vyāsas tathātreyo dīptimanto bahuśrutāḥ
bhāradvājas tathā drauṇir aśvatthāmā mahādyutiḥ //
5.d:
रामो व्यासस् तथात्रेयो दीप्तिमन्तो बहुश्रुताः
भारद्वाजस् तथा द्रौणिर् अश्वत्थामा महाद्युतिः ॥
5.m: Rāma, Vyāsa, and the son of Atri, radiant and very learned; / the descendant of Bharadvāja, and the son of Droṇa, Aśvatthāman of great splendour;

5.s:
gautamaś cājaraś caiva śaradvān nāma gautamaḥ
kauśiko gālavaś caiva aurvaḥ kāśyapa eva ca //
5.d:
गौतमश् चाजरश् चैव शरद्वान् नाम गौतमः
कौशिको गालवश् चैव और्वः काश्यप एव च ॥
5.m: Gautama, the ageless Gautama named Śaradvant; / the descendant of Kuśika, Gālava, and Aurva son of Kaśyapa—

5.s:
ete sapta mahātmāno bhaviṣyā munisattamāḥ
vairī caivādhvarīvāṃś ca śamano dhṛtimān vasuḥ //
5.d:
एते सप्त महात्मानो भविष्या मुनिसत्तमाः
वैरी चैवाध्वरीवांश् च शमनो धृतिमान् वसुः ॥
5.m: these seven great-souled ones are the future [sages], O best of sages. / Vairin, Adhvarīvat, Śamana, Dhṛtimat, Vasu,

5.s:
ariṣṭaś cāpy adhṛṣṭaś ca vājī sumatir eva ca
sāvarṇasya manoḥ putrā bhaviṣyā munisattamāḥ //
5.d:
अरिष्टश् चाप्य् अधृष्टश् च वाजी सुमतिर् एव च
सावर्णस्य मनोः पुत्रा भविष्या मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
5.m: Ariṣṭa, Adhṛṣṭa, Vājin, and Sumati— / these are the future sons of Sāvarṇi Manu, O best of sages.

5.s:
eteṣāṃ kalyam utthāya kīrtanāt sukham edhate
yaśaś cāpnoti sumahad āyuṣmāṃś ca bhaven naraḥ //
5.d:
एतेषां कल्यम् उत्थाय कीर्तनात् सुखम् एधते
यशश् चाप्नोति सुमहद् आयुष्मांश् च भवेन् नरः ॥
5.m: By reciting their names upon rising at dawn, a person thrives in happiness, / attains exceedingly great renown, and becomes long-lived.

5.s:
etāny uktāni bho viprāḥ sapta sapta ca tattvataḥ
manvantarāṇi saṃkṣepāc chṛṇutānāgatāny api //
5.d:
एतान्य् उक्तानि भो विप्राः सप्त सप्त च तत्त्वतः
मन्वन्तराणि संक्षेपाच् छृणुतानागतान्य् अपि ॥
5.m: These seven and seven manvantaras have been told in truth, O twice-born; / hear also briefly about the future ones.

5.s:
sāvarṇā manavo viprāḥ pañca tāṃś ca nibodhata
eko vaivasvatas teṣāṃ catvāras tu prajāpateḥ //
5.d:
सावर्णा मनवो विप्राः पञ्च तांश् च निबोधत
एको वैवस्वतस् तेषां चत्वारस् तु प्रजापतेः ॥
5.m: The Sāvarṇa Manus are five, O twice-born; learn of them: / one of them belongs to Vivasvat, and four belong to the lord of creatures.

5.s:
parameṣṭhisutā viprā merusāvarṇyatāṃ gatāḥ
dakṣasyaite hi dauhitrāḥ priyāyās tanayā nṛpāḥ //
5.d:
परमेष्ठिसुता विप्रा मेरुसावर्ण्यतां गताः
दक्षस्यैते हि दौहित्राः प्रियायास् तनया नृपाः ॥
5.m: Sons of Parameṣṭhin, O twice-born, who attained likeness with Meru, / these royal sons of Priyā are the daughter's sons of Dakṣa,

5.s:
mahatā tapasā yuktā merupṛṣṭhe mahaujasaḥ
ruceḥ prajāpateḥ putro raucyo nāma manuḥ smṛtaḥ //
5.d:
महता तपसा युक्ता मेरुपृष्ठे महौजसः
रुचेः प्रजापतेः पुत्रो रौच्यो नाम मनुः स्मृतः ॥
5.m: endowed with great ascetic heat, of great luster, on the ridge of Meru. / The son of Ruci, the lord of creatures, is remembered as the Manu named Raucya.

5.s:
bhūtyāṃ cotpādito devyāṃ bhautyo nāma ruceḥ sutaḥ
anāgatāś ca saptaite kalpe 'smin manavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
5.d:
भूत्यां चोत्पादितो देव्यां भौत्यो नाम रुचेः सुतः
अनागताश् च सप्तैते कल्पे ऽस्मिन् मनवः स्मृताः ॥
5.m: And born of the goddess Bhūti is Ruci's son named Bhautya. / These seven are remembered as the future Manus in this kalpa.

5.s:
tair iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā
pūrṇaṃ yugasahasraṃ tu paripālyā dvijottamāḥ //
5.d:
तैर् इयं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना
पूर्णं युगसहस्रं तु परिपाल्या द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
5.m: By them this entire earth with its seven continents and cities / is to be protected for a full thousand yugas, O best of twice-born.

5.s:
prajāpatiś ca tapasā saṃhāraṃ teṣu nityaśaḥ
yugāni saptatis tāni sāgrāṇi kathitāni ca //
5.d:
प्रजापतिश् च तपसा संहारं तेषु नित्यशः
युगानि सप्ततिस् तानि साग्राणि कथितानि च ॥
5.m: And the lord of creatures constantly effects dissolution among them by ascetic heat; / seventy yugas and somewhat more are stated

5.s:
kṛtatretādiyuktāni manor antaram ucyate
caturdaśaite manavaḥ kathitāḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ //
5.d:
कृतत्रेतादियुक्तानि मनोर् अन्तरम् उच्यते
चतुर्दशैते मनवः कथिताः कीर्तिवर्धनाः ॥
5.m: with their Kṛta, Tretā, and other [ages]; this is called the period of a Manu. / These fourteen Manus are declared to increase renown.

5.s:
vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu sarveṣu prabhaviṣṇavaḥ
prajānāṃ patayo viprā dhanyam eṣāṃ prakīrtanam //
5.d:
वेदेषु सपुराणेषु सर्वेषु प्रभविष्णवः
प्रजानां पतयो विप्रा धन्यम् एषां प्रकीर्तनम् ॥
5.m: Mighty rulers throughout all Vedas and Purāṇas, / lords of creatures, O twice-born—auspicious is their recitation.

5.s:
manvantareṣu saṃhārāḥ saṃhārānteṣu saṃbhavāḥ
na śakyate 'ntas teṣāṃ vai vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api //
5.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु संहाराः संहारान्तेषु संभवाः
न शक्यते ऽन्तस् तेषां वै वक्तुं वर्षशतैर् अपि ॥
5.m: There are dissolutions within the manvantaras, and creations at the end of the dissolutions; / it is not possible to describe their end even in a hundred years,

5.s:
visargasya prajānāṃ vai saṃhārasya ca bho dvijāḥ
manvantareṣu saṃhārāḥ śrūyante dvijasattamāḥ //
5.d:
विसर्गस्य प्रजानां वै संहारस्य च भो द्विजाः
मन्वन्तरेषु संहाराः श्रूयन्ते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
5.m: both of the emission of creatures, O twice-born, and of their dissolution; / dissolutions within the manvantaras are heard of, O best of twice-born.

5.s:
saśeṣās tatra tiṣṭhanti devāḥ saptarṣibhiḥ saha
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śrutena ca samanvitāḥ //
5.d:
सशेषास् तत्र तिष्ठन्ति देवाः सप्तर्षिभिः सह
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रुतेन च समन्विताः ॥
5.m: The gods remain there with a remainder, together with the seven sages, / endowed with ascetic power, celibacy, and learning.

5.s:
pūrṇe yugasahasre tu kalpo niḥśeṣa ucyate
tatra bhūtāni sarvāṇi dagdhāny ādityaraśmibhiḥ //
5.d:
पूर्णे युगसहस्रे तु कल्पो निःशेष उच्यते
तत्र भूतानि सर्वाणि दग्धान्य् आदित्यरश्मिभिः ॥
5.m: When a thousand yugas are completed, the kalpa is said to come to an end; / then all beings are burned by the rays of the sun.

5.s:
brahmāṇam agrataḥ kṛtvā sahādityagaṇair dvijāḥ
praviśanti suraśreṣṭhaṃ harinārāyaṇaṃ prabhum //
5.d:
ब्रह्माणम् अग्रतः कृत्वा सहादित्यगणैर् द्विजाः
प्रविशन्ति सुरश्रेष्ठं हरिनारायणं प्रभुम् ॥
5.m: Placing Brahmā at their head, along with the groups of Ādityas, O twice-born ones, / they enter the lord Hari-Nārāyaṇa, the best of the gods,

5.s:
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kalpānteṣu punaḥ punaḥ
avyaktaḥ śāśvato devas tasya sarvam idaṃ jagat //
5.d:
स्रष्टारं सर्वभूतानां कल्पान्तेषु पुनः पुनः
अव्यक्तः शाश्वतो देवस् तस्य सर्वम् इदं जगत् ॥
5.m: the creator of all beings, again and again at the ends of kalpas. / The god is unmanifest and eternal; this whole world belongs to him.

5.s:
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi manor vaivasvatasya vai
visargaṃ muniśārdūlāḥ sāṃpratasya mahādyuteḥ //
5.d:
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि मनोर् वैवस्वतस्य वै
विसर्गं मुनिशार्दूलाः सांप्रतस्य महाद्युतेः ॥
5.m: Here I shall proclaim to you the creation of Manu Vaivasvata, / O tigers among sages, of the present one of great splendor,

5.s:
atra vaṃśaprasaṅgena kathyamānaṃ purātanam
yatrotpanno mahātmā sa harir vṛṣṇikule prabhuḥ //
5.d:
अत्र वंशप्रसङ्गेन कथ्यमानं पुरातनम्
यत्रोत्पन्नो महात्मा स हरिर् वृष्णिकुले प्रभुः ॥
5.m: as it is told in ancient lore in connection with the lineage, / wherein that great-souled lord Hari was born into the Vṛṣṇi race.

6.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
vivasvān kaśyapāj jajñe dākṣāyaṇyāṃ dvijottamāḥ
tasya bhāryābhavat saṃjñā tvāṣṭrī devī vivasvataḥ //
6.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
विवस्वान् कश्यपाज् जज्ञे दाक्षायण्यां द्विजोत्तमाः
तस्य भार्याभवत् संज्ञा त्वाष्ट्री देवी विवस्वतः ॥
6.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Vivasvat was born from Kaśyapa through the daughter of Dakṣa, O best of the twice-born; / Vivasvat's wife was goddess Saṃjñā, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ.

6.s:
sureśvarīti vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu bhāvinī
sā vai bhāryā bhagavato mārtaṇḍasya mahātmanaḥ //
6.d:
सुरेश्वरीति विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु भाविनी
सा वै भार्या भगवतो मार्तण्डस्य महात्मनः ॥
6.m: Renowned in the three worlds as the noble lady Sureśvarī, / she was indeed the wife of the lord, the great-souled Mārtaṇḍa.

6.s:
bhartṛrūpeṇa nātuṣyad rūpayauvanaśālinī
saṃjñā nāma sutapasā sudīptena samanvitā //
6.d:
भर्तृरूपेण नातुष्यद् रूपयौवनशालिनी
संज्ञा नाम सुतपसा सुदीप्तेन समन्विता ॥
6.m: Endowed with beauty and youth, Saṃjñā by name, / and possessed of great, blazing ascetic power, she was not pleased with her husband's form.

6.s:
ādityasya hi tad rūpaṃ maṇḍalasya sutejasā
gātreṣu paridagdhaṃ vai nātikāntam ivābhavat //
6.d:
आदित्यस्य हि तद् रूपं मण्डलस्य सुतेजसा
गात्रेषु परिदग्धं वै नातिकान्तम् इवाभवत् ॥
6.m: For that form of the sun's orb, burnt upon his limbs / by his intense brilliance, seemed not very lovely.

6.s:
na khalv ayaṃ mṛto 'ṇḍasya iti snehād abhāṣata
ajānan kāśyapas tasmān mārtaṇḍa iti cocyate //
6.d:
न खल्व् अयं मृतो ऽण्डस्य इति स्नेहाद् अभाषत
अजानन् काश्यपस् तस्मान् मार्तण्ड इति चोच्यते ॥
6.m: Kaśyapa, not knowing, out of affection said: / 'Surely this [child] of the egg is not dead (mṛto 'ṇḍasya)?' Hence he is called Mārtaṇḍa.

6.s:
tejas tv abhyadhikaṃ tasya nityam eva vivasvataḥ
yenātitāpayām āsa trīṃl lokān kaśyapātmajaḥ //
6.d:
तेजस् त्व् अभ्यधिकं तस्य नित्यम् एव विवस्वतः
येनातितापयाम् आस त्रींल् लोकान् कश्यपात्मजः ॥
6.m: And the splendor of Vivasvat was ever excessive, / with which the son of Kaśyapa caused the three worlds to burn intensely.

6.s:
trīṇy apatyāni bho viprāḥ saṃjñāyāṃ tapatāṃ varaḥ
ādityo janayām āsa kanyāṃ dvau ca prajāpatī //
6.d:
त्रीण्य् अपत्यानि भो विप्राः संज्ञायां तपतां वरः
आदित्यो जनयाम् आस कन्यां द्वौ च प्रजापती ॥
6.m: Upon Saṃjñā, O vipras, the sun, best of burning ones, / fathered three offspring: a daughter and two lords of creatures.

6.s:
manur vaivasvataḥ pūrvaṃ śrāddhadevaḥ prajāpatiḥ
yamaś ca yamunā caiva yamajau saṃbabhūvatuḥ //
6.d:
मनुर् वैवस्वतः पूर्वं श्राद्धदेवः प्रजापतिः
यमश् च यमुना चैव यमजौ संबभूवतुः ॥
6.m: First was Manu Vaivasvata, the lord of creatures Śrāddhadeva; / and twins were born: Yama and Yamunā.

6.s:
śyāmavarṇaṃ tu tad rūpaṃ saṃjñā dṛṣṭvā vivasvataḥ
asahantī tu svāṃ chāyāṃ savarṇāṃ nirmame tataḥ //
6.d:
श्यामवर्णं तु तद् रूपं संज्ञा दृष्ट्वा विवस्वतः
असहन्ती तु स्वां छायां सवर्णां निर्ममे ततः ॥
6.m: Seeing that dark-colored form of Vivasvat, / unable to endure it, Saṃjñā then created her own shadow, of like appearance (Savarṇā).

6.s:
māyāmayī tu sā saṃjñā tasyāṃ chāyāsamutthitām
prāñjaliḥ praṇatā bhūtvā chāyā saṃjñāṃ dvijottamāḥ //
6.d:
मायामयी तु सा संज्ञा तस्यां छायासमुत्थिताम्
प्राञ्जलिः प्रणता भूत्वा छाया संज्ञां द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
6.m: Created by illusory power, that shadow arose from her as Saṃjñā. / Joining her palms and bowing down to Saṃjñā, O best of the twice-born,

6.s:
uvāca kiṃ mayā kāryaṃ kathayasva śucismite
sthitāsmi tava nirdeśe śādhi māṃ varavarṇini //
6.d:
उवाच किं मया कार्यं कथयस्व शुचिस्मिते
स्थितास्मि तव निर्देशे शाधि मां वरवर्णिनि ॥
6.m: the shadow said: 'Tell me, O sweet-smiling one, what must I do? / I stand at your command; instruct me, O fair-complexioned lady.'

6.s:
saṃjñovāca
ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhadraṃ te svam eva bhavanaṃ pituḥ
tvayaiva bhavane mahyaṃ vastavyaṃ nirviśaṅkayā //
6.d:
संज्ञोवाच
अहं यास्यामि भद्रं ते स्वम् एव भवनं पितुः
त्वयैव भवने मह्यं वस्तव्यं निर्विशङ्कया ॥
6.m: Saṃjñā said: / 'Blessings to you! I shall go to my own father's dwelling. / You must live in my abode without any hesitation,

6.s:
imau ca bālakau mahyaṃ kanyā ceyaṃ sumadhyamā
saṃbhāvyās te na cākhyeyam idaṃ bhagavate kvacit //
6.d:
इमौ च बालकौ मह्यं कन्या चेयं सुमध्यमा
संभाव्यास् ते न चाख्येयम् इदं भगवते क्वचित् ॥
6.m: and these two young boys of mine and this slender-waisted maiden / must be cherished by you, and this must never be told to the lord.'

6.s:
savarṇovāca
ā kacagrahaṇād devi ā śāpān naiva karhicit
ākhyāsyāmi namas tubhyaṃ gaccha devi yathāsukham //
6.d:
सवर्णोवाच
आ कचग्रहणाद् देवि आ शापान् नैव कर्हिचित्
आख्यास्यामि नमस् तुभ्यं गच्छ देवि यथासुखम् ॥
6.m: Savarṇā said: / 'O goddess, until seized by the hair, until cursed, / I shall never tell. Homage to you; go at your pleasure, O goddess.'

6.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
samādiśya savarṇāṃ tu tathety uktā tayā ca sā
tvaṣṭuḥ samīpam agamad vrīḍiteva tapasvinī //
6.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
समादिश्य सवर्णां तु तथेत्य् उक्ता तया च सा
त्वष्टुः समीपम् अगमद् व्रीडितेव तपस्विनी ॥
6.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Having thus instructed Savarṇā, and having been told 'So be it' by her, / the ascetic woman went to Tvaṣṭṛ as though ashamed.

6.s:
pituḥ samīpagā sā tu pitrā nirbhartsitā śubhā
bhartuḥ samīpaṃ gaccheti niyuktā ca punaḥ punaḥ //
6.d:
पितुः समीपगा सा तु पित्रा निर्भर्त्सिता शुभा
भर्तुः समीपं गच्छेति नियुक्ता च पुनः पुनः ॥
6.m: Having arrived near her father, the auspicious lady was scolded by her father / and told repeatedly: 'Go to your husband.'

6.s:
āgacchad vaḍavā bhūtvā ācchādya rūpam aninditā
kurūn athottarān gatvā tṛṇāny atha cacāra ha //
6.d:
आगच्छद् वडवा भूत्वा आच्छाद्य रूपम् अनिन्दिता
कुरून् अथोत्तरान् गत्वा तृणान्य् अथ चचार ह ॥
6.m: Becoming a mare and concealing her form, the blameless woman departed; / having gone to the Northern Kurus, she grazed on grass.

6.s:
dvitīyāyāṃ tu saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñeyam iti cintayan
ādityo janayām āsa putram ātmasamaṃ tadā //
6.d:
द्वितीयायां तु संज्ञायां संज्ञेयम् इति चिन्तयन्
आदित्यो जनयाम् आस पुत्रम् आत्मसमं तदा ॥
6.m: Thinking 'This is Saṃjñā,' the sun then begot / upon the second Saṃjñā a son equal to himself.

6.s:
pūrvajasya manor viprāḥ sadṛśo 'yam iti prabhuḥ
manur evābhavan nāmnā sāvarṇa iti cocyate //
6.d:
पूर्वजस्य मनोर् विप्राः सदृशो ऽयम् इति प्रभुः
मनुर् एवाभवन् नाम्ना सावर्ण इति चोच्यते ॥
6.m: Thinking 'He is like his elder brother Manu,' O vipras, the lord [named him] / Manu indeed by name, and he is called Sāvarṇa.

6.s:
dvitīyo yaḥ sutas tasyāḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śanaiścaraḥ
saṃjñā tu pārthivī viprāḥ svasya putrasya vai tadā //
6.d:
द्वितीयो यः सुतस् तस्याः स विज्ञेयः शनैश्चरः
संज्ञा तु पार्थिवी विप्राः स्वस्य पुत्रस्य वै तदा ॥
6.m: Her second son is to be known as Śanaiścara. / Then the earthly Saṃjñā, O vipras, showed excessive affection

6.s:
cakārābhyadhikaṃ snehaṃ na tathā pūrvajeṣu vai
manus tasyāḥ kṣamat tat tu yamas tasyā na cakṣame //
6.d:
चकाराभ्यधिकं स्नेहं न तथा पूर्वजेषु वै
मनुस् तस्याः क्षमत् तत् तु यमस् तस्या न चक्षमे ॥
6.m: for her own son, and not in that way toward the older children. / Manu tolerated that of hers, but Yama did not tolerate it.

6.s:
sa vai roṣāc ca bālyāc ca bhāvino 'rthasya vānagha
padā saṃtarjayām āsa saṃjñāṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ //
6.d:
स वै रोषाच् च बाल्याच् च भाविनो ऽर्थस्य वानघ
पदा संतर्जयाम् आस संज्ञां वैवस्वतो यमः ॥
6.m: Through anger, through childishness, and through the impending fate, O sinless one, / Yama Vaivasvata threatened Saṃjñā with his foot.

6.s:
taṃ śaśāpa tataḥ krodhāt sāvarṇajananī tadā
caraṇaḥ patatām eṣa taveti bhṛśaduḥkhitā //
6.d:
तं शशाप ततः क्रोधात् सावर्णजननी तदा
चरणः पतताम् एष तवेति भृशदुःखिता ॥
6.m: Then, out of rage, the mother of Sāvarṇa, deeply grieved, / cursed him: 'May this foot of yours fall off!'

6.s:
yamas tu tat pituḥ sarvaṃ prāñjaliḥ pratyavedayat
bhṛśaṃ śāpabhayodvignaḥ saṃjñāvākyair viśaṅkitaḥ //
6.d:
यमस् तु तत् पितुः सर्वं प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्यवेदयत्
भृशं शापभयोद्विग्नः संज्ञावाक्यैर् विशङ्कितः ॥
6.m: Yama, with joined palms, reported everything to his father, / deeply agitated by fear of the curse, anxious over Saṃjñā's words.

6.s:
śāpo 'yaṃ vinivarteta provāca pitaraṃ dvijāḥ
mātrā snehena sarveṣu vartitavyaṃ suteṣu vai //
6.d:
शापो ऽयं विनिवर्तेत प्रोवाच पितरं द्विजाः
मात्रा स्नेहेन सर्वेषु वर्तितव्यं सुतेषु वै ॥
6.m: He said to his father, O twice-born ones: 'May this curse be averted! / A mother should behave with affection toward all her sons.

6.s:
seyam asmān apāsyeha vivasvan saṃbubhūṣati
tasyāṃ mayodyataḥ pādo na tu dehe nipātitaḥ //
6.d:
सेयम् अस्मान् अपास्येह विवस्वन् संबुभूषति
तस्यां मयोद्यतः पादो न तु देहे निपातितः ॥
6.m: Casting us aside here, O Vivasvat, she wishes to be [only with hers]. / My foot was raised against her, but not dropped upon her body.

6.s:
bālyād vā yadi vā laulyān mohāt tat kṣantum arhasi
śapto 'ham asmi lokeśa jananyā tapatāṃ vara
tava prasādāc caraṇo na paten mama gopate //
6.d:
बाल्याद् वा यदि वा लौल्यान् मोहात् तत् क्षन्तुम् अर्हसि
शप्तो ऽहम् अस्मि लोकेश जनन्या तपतां वर
तव प्रसादाच् चरणो न पतेन् मम गोपते ॥
6.m: Whether from childishness, or from fickleness, or through delusion, you ought to forgive it. / I have been cursed by my mother, O lord of the world, best of scorching ones! / Through your favor, may my foot not fall off, O lord of rays!'

6.s:
vivasvān uvāca
asaṃśayaṃ putra mahad bhaviṣyaty atra kāraṇam
yena tvām āviśat krodho dharmajñaṃ satyavādinam //
6.d:
विवस्वान् उवाच
असंशयं पुत्र महद् भविष्यत्य् अत्र कारणम्
येन त्वाम् आविशत् क्रोधो धर्मज्ञं सत्यवादिनम् ॥
6.m: Vivasvat said: / 'Undoubtedly, my son, there must be a great reason in this, / whereby anger entered you, who know dharma and speak the truth.

6.s:
na śakyam etan mithyā tu kartuṃ mātṛvacas tava
kṛmayo māṃsam ādāya yāsyanty avanim eva ca //
6.d:
न शक्यम् एतन् मिथ्या तु कर्तुं मातृवचस् तव
कृमयो मांसम् आदाय यास्यन्त्य् अवनिम् एव च ॥
6.m: Yet your mother's word cannot be rendered false: / worms, having taken [some] flesh, will go into the earth.

6.s:
kṛtam evaṃ vacas tathyaṃ mātus tava bhaviṣyati
śāpasya parihāreṇa tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi //
6.d:
कृतम् एवं वचस् तथ्यं मातुस् तव भविष्यति
शापस्य परिहारेण त्वं च त्रातो भविष्यसि ॥
6.m: Thus your mother's word will become true, / and through the mitigation of the curse you will be saved.'

6.s:
ādityaś cābravīt saṃjñāṃ kimarthaṃ tanayeṣu vai
tulyeṣv abhyadhikaḥ sneha ekasmin kriyate tvayā //
6.d:
आदित्यश् चाब्रवीत् संज्ञां किमर्थं तनयेषु वै
तुल्येष्व् अभ्यधिकः स्नेह एकस्मिन् क्रियते त्वया ॥
6.m: The sun then said to Saṃjñā: 'Why is it that, among children / who are equal, greater affection is shown by you toward one?'

6.s:
sā tat pariharantī tu nācacakṣe vivasvate
sa cātmānaṃ samādhāya yogāt tathyam apaśyata //
6.d:
सा तत् परिहरन्ती तु नाचचक्षे विवस्वते
स चात्मानं समाधाय योगात् तथ्यम् अपश्यत ॥
6.m: Evading that, she did not explain to Vivasvat. / And concentrating himself, through yoga he saw the truth.

6.s:
tāṃ śaptukāmo bhagavān nāśapan munisattamāḥ
mūrdhajeṣu nijagrāha sa tu tāṃ munisattamāḥ //
6.d:
तां शप्तुकामो भगवान् नाशपन् मुनिसत्तमाः
मूर्धजेषु निजग्राह स तु तां मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
6.m: Wishing to curse her, the lord did not curse her, O best of sages; / but he seized her by the hair, O best of sages.

6.s:
tataḥ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ācacakṣe vivasvate
vivasvān atha tac chrutvā kruddhas tvaṣṭāram abhyagāt //
6.d:
ततः सर्वं यथावृत्तम् आचचक्षे विवस्वते
विवस्वान् अथ तच् छ्रुत्वा क्रुद्धस् त्वष्टारम् अभ्यगात् ॥
6.m: Then she told Vivasvat everything as it had happened. / Hearing that, Vivasvat went angrily to Tvaṣṭṛ.

6.s:
dṛṣṭvā tu taṃ yathānyāyam arcayitvā vibhāvasum
nirdagdhukāmaṃ roṣeṇa sāntvayām āsa vai tadā //
6.d:
दृष्ट्वा तु तं यथान्यायम् अर्चयित्वा विभावसुम्
निर्दग्धुकामं रोषेण सान्त्वयाम् आस वै तदा ॥
6.m: Seeing him and honoring the fire-like sun according to custom, / [Tvaṣṭṛ] then consoled him who wished to burn [everything] in his fury.

6.s:
tvaṣṭovāca
tavātitejasāviṣṭam idaṃ rūpaṃ na śobhate
asahantī ca saṃjñā sā vane carati śāḍvale //
6.d:
त्वष्टोवाच
तवातितेजसाविष्टम् इदं रूपं न शोभते
असहन्ती च संज्ञा सा वने चरति शाड्वले ॥
6.m: Tvaṣṭṛ said: / 'This form of yours, pervaded by excessive radiance, is not pleasant; / and unable to endure it, that Saṃjñā wanders in a grassy forest.

6.s:
draṣṭā hi tāṃ bhavān adya svāṃ bhāryāṃ śubhacāriṇīm
ślāghyāṃ yogabalopetāṃ yogam āsthāya gopate //
6.d:
द्रष्टा हि तां भवान् अद्य स्वां भार्यां शुभचारिणीम्
श्लाघ्यां योगबलोपेतां योगम् आस्थाय गोपते ॥
6.m: For today, taking recourse to yoga, O lord of rays, you shall see her, / your wife of auspicious conduct, praiseworthy and endowed with yogic power.

6.s:
anukūlaṃ tu te deva yadi syān mama saṃmatam
rūpaṃ nirvartayāmy adya tava kāntam ariṃdama //
6.d:
अनुकूलं तु ते देव यदि स्यान् मम संमतम्
रूपं निर्वर्तयाम्य् अद्य तव कान्तम् अरिंदम ॥
6.m: If it is agreeable to you, O god, and according to my opinion, / today I shall fashion a lovely form for you, O subduer of foes.'

6.s:
tato 'bhyupagamāt tvaṣṭā mārtaṇḍasya vivasvataḥ
bhramim āropya tat tejaḥ śātayām āsa bho dvijāḥ //
6.d:
ततो ऽभ्युपगमात् त्वष्टा मार्तण्डस्य विवस्वतः
भ्रमिम् आरोप्य तत् तेजः शातयाम् आस भो द्विजाः ॥
6.m: Then, with his consent, Tvaṣṭṛ placed the brilliance of Mārtaṇḍa Vivasvat / on a lathe and pared it down, O twice-born ones.

6.s:
tato nirbhāsitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasā saṃhatena vai
kāntāt kāntataraṃ draṣṭum adhikaṃ śuśubhe tadā //
6.d:
ततो निर्भासितं रूपं तेजसा संहतेन वै
कान्तात् कान्ततरं द्रष्टुम् अधिकं शुशुभे तदा ॥
6.m: Then his form, illuminated with concentrated brilliance / and lovelier than lovely, shone exceedingly to behold.

6.s:
dadarśa yogam āsthāya svāṃ bhāryāṃ vaḍavāṃ tataḥ
adhṛṣyāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tejasā niyamena ca //
6.d:
ददर्श योगम् आस्थाय स्वां भार्यां वडवां ततः
अधृष्यां सर्वभूतानां तेजसा नियमेन च ॥
6.m: Then, having resorted to yoga, he saw his wife as a mare, / unassailable to all creatures by her splendour and restraint.

6.s:
vaḍavāvapuṣā viprāś carantīm akutobhayām
so 'śvarūpeṇa bhagavāṃs tāṃ mukhe samabhāvayat //
6.d:
वडवावपुषा विप्राश् चरन्तीम् अकुतोभयाम्
सो ऽश्वरूपेण भगवांस् तां मुखे समभावयत् ॥
6.m: Roaming in the form of a mare, O brahmins, fearing nothing from any quarter. / Assuming the form of a horse, the blessed lord met her mouth to mouth.

6.s:
maithunāya viceṣṭantīṃ parapuṃso 'vaśaṅkayā
sā tan niravamac chukraṃ nāsikābhyāṃ vivasvataḥ //
6.d:
मैथुनाय विचेष्टन्तीं परपुंसो ऽवशङ्कया
सा तन् निरवमच् छुक्रं नासिकाभ्यां विवस्वतः ॥
6.m: As she struggled against union, suspecting him to be another male, / she expelled that semen of Vivasvat through both her nostrils.

6.s:
devau tasyām ajāyetām aśvinau bhiṣajāṃ varau
nāsatyaś caiva dasraś ca smṛtau dvāv aśvināv iti //
6.d:
देवौ तस्याम् अजायेताम् अश्विनौ भिषजां वरौ
नासत्यश् चैव दस्रश् च स्मृतौ द्वाव् अश्विनाव् इति ॥
6.m: From her were born the two gods, the Aśvins, best among physicians; / they are remembered as two Aśvins, Nāsatya and Dasra.

6.s:
mārtaṇḍasyātmajāv etāv aṣṭamasya prajāpateḥ
tāṃ tu rūpeṇa kāntena darśayām āsa bhāskaraḥ //
6.d:
मार्तण्डस्यात्मजाव् एताव् अष्टमस्य प्रजापतेः
तां तु रूपेण कान्तेन दर्शयाम् आस भास्करः ॥
6.m: These two were sons of Mārtaṇḍa, the eighth lord of creatures. / Then the sun showed himself to her in his lovely form.

6.s:
sā tu dṛṣṭvaiva bhartāraṃ tutoṣa munisattamāḥ
yamas tu karmaṇā tena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasaḥ //
6.d:
सा तु दृष्ट्वैव भर्तारं तुतोष मुनिसत्तमाः
यमस् तु कर्मणा तेन भृशं पीडितमानसः ॥
6.m: Upon seeing her husband, O best of sages, she was delighted. / But Yama, his mind severely tormented by that deed,

6.s:
dharmeṇa rañjayām āsa dharmarāja imāḥ prajāḥ
sa lebhe karmaṇā tena śubhena paramadyutiḥ //
6.d:
धर्मेण रञ्जयाम् आस धर्मराज इमाः प्रजाः
स लेभे कर्मणा तेन शुभेन परमद्युतिः ॥
6.m: gladdened these creatures through dharma, becoming the King of Dharma. / By that auspicious conduct, he, possessed of supreme radiance, attained

6.s:
pitṝṇām ādhipatyaṃ ca lokapālatvam eva ca
manuḥ prajāpatis tv āsīt sāvarṇiḥ sa tapodhanāḥ //
6.d:
पितॄणाम् आधिपत्यं च लोकपालत्वम् एव च
मनुः प्रजापतिस् त्व् आसीत् सावर्णिः स तपोधनाः ॥
6.m: sovereignty over the ancestors and the status of a world-guardian. / And the lord of creatures Manu Sāvarṇi, O rich in asceticism,

6.s:
bhāvyaḥ samāgate tasmin manuḥ sāvarṇike 'ntare
merupṛṣṭhe tapo nityam adyāpi sa caraty uta //
6.d:
भाव्यः समागते तस्मिन् मनुः सावर्णिके ऽन्तरे
मेरुपृष्ठे तपो नित्यम् अद्यापि स चरत्य् उत ॥
6.m: is to be the Manu in that future Sāvarṇika interval; / even today he perpetually performs austerities on the summit of Meru.

6.s:
bhrātā śanaiścaras tasya grahatvaṃ sa tu labdhavān
tvaṣṭā tu tejasā tena viṣṇoś cakram akalpayat //
6.d:
भ्राता शनैश्चरस् तस्य ग्रहत्वं स तु लब्धवान्
त्वष्टा तु तेजसा तेन विष्णोश् चक्रम् अकल्पयत् ॥
6.m: His brother Śanaiścara attained the status of a planet. / With that splendour Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the discus of Viṣṇu,

6.s:
tad apratihataṃ yuddhe dānavāntacikīrṣayā
yavīyasī tu sāpy āsīd yamī kanyā yaśasvinī //
6.d:
तद् अप्रतिहतं युद्धे दानवान्तचिकीर्षया
यवीयसी तु साप्य् आसीद् यमी कन्या यशस्विनी ॥
6.m: which is unhindered in battle, with the wish to destroy the Dānavas. / There was also a younger daughter, the renowned Yamī;

6.s:
abhavac ca saricchreṣṭhā yamunā lokapāvanī
manur ity ucyate loke sāvarṇa iti cocyate //
6.d:
अभवच् च सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यमुना लोकपावनी
मनुर् इत्य् उच्यते लोके सावर्ण इति चोच्यते ॥
6.m: she became the foremost of rivers, Yamunā, purifier of the world. / He is called Manu in the world, and he is also called Sāvarṇa.

6.s:
dvitīyo yaḥ sutas tasya manor bhrātā śanaiścaraḥ
grahatvaṃ sa ca lebhe vai sarvalokābhipūjitaḥ //
6.d:
द्वितीयो यः सुतस् तस्य मनोर् भ्राता शनैश्चरः
ग्रहत्वं स च लेभे वै सर्वलोकाभिपूजितः ॥
6.m: His second son, Śanaiścara, the brother of that Manu, / attained the status of a planet, worshipped by all worlds.

6.s:
ya idaṃ janma devānāṃ śṛṇuyān narasattamaḥ
āpadaṃ prāpya mucyeta prāpnuyāc ca mahad yaśaḥ //
6.d:
य इदं जन्म देवानां शृणुयान् नरसत्तमः
आपदं प्राप्य मुच्येत प्राप्नुयाच् च महद् यशः ॥
6.m: The best among men who hears this birth of the gods / is freed if fallen into distress and attains great renown.

7.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
manor vaivasvatasyāsan putrā vai nava tatsamāḥ
ikṣvākuś caiva nābhāgo dhṛṣṭaḥ śaryātir eva ca //
7.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
मनोर् वैवस्वतस्यासन् पुत्रा वै नव तत्समाः
इक्ष्वाकुश् चैव नाभागो धृष्टः शर्यातिर् एव च ॥
7.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / The sons of Manu Vaivasvata were nine, equal to him: / Ikṣvāku, Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti,

7.s:
nariṣyantaś ca ṣaṣṭho vai prāṃśū riṣṭaś ca saptamaḥ
karūṣaś ca pṛṣadhraś ca navaite munisattamāḥ //
7.d:
नरिष्यन्तश् च षष्ठो वै प्रांशू रिष्टश् च सप्तमः
करूषश् च पृषध्रश् च नवैते मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
7.m: and Nariṣyanta, the sixth Prāṃśu, and Riṣṭa the seventh, / and Karūṣa and Pṛṣadhra: these nine, O best of sages.

7.s:
akarot putrakāmas tu manur iṣṭiṃ prajāpatiḥ
mitrāvaruṇayor viprāḥ pūrvam eva mahāmatiḥ //
7.d:
अकरोत् पुत्रकामस् तु मनुर् इष्टिं प्रजापतिः
मित्रावरुणयोर् विप्राः पूर्वम् एव महामतिः ॥
7.m: Desiring sons, the lord of creatures Manu, of great intellect, / had earlier performed an offering to Mitra and Varuṇa, O brahmins,

7.s:
anutpanneṣu bahuṣu putreṣv eteṣu bho dvijāḥ
tasyāṃ ca vartamānāyām iṣṭyāṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ //
7.d:
अनुत्पन्नेषु बहुषु पुत्रेष्व् एतेषु भो द्विजाः
तस्यां च वर्तमानायाम् इष्ट्यां च द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
7.m: before these many sons were born, O twice-born. / And while that offering was being performed, O best of the twice-born,

7.s:
mitrāvaruṇayor aṃśe manur āhutim āvahat
tatra divyāmbaradharā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā //
7.d:
मित्रावरुणयोर् अंशे मनुर् आहुतिम् आवहत्
तत्र दिव्याम्बरधरा दिव्याभरणभूषिता ॥
7.m: Manu made an oblation to the share of Mitra and Varuṇa. / There, wearing celestial garments and adorned with celestial ornaments,

7.s:
divyasaṃhananā caiva ilā jajña iti śrutiḥ
